candidates.name: Remove O.__releaseChrome from LibKa0s/OptionsTabs.lua (Options major, OptionsTabs minor 8 -> 9)
candidates.rationale: This is a removal, not a promotion, so the question is whether anything reaches the export. Nothing does. The file-local releaseChrome stays because PageBanner (OptionsTabs.lua:943) and the page render (:1036) call it. Only the instance-table export at :636 goes. It is assigned per instance inside lib.__AttachTabs(O, d) (:457), so the export never sits on the shared lib table and cannot be left behind on an upgraded copy. No library suite calls it: tests/test_options_tabs.lua:827 names releaseChrome only in a comment. A scan of every O.__* assignment in LibKa0s/Options*.lua against LibKa0s/, tests/ and testkit/ found this as the only dead Options internal. In the 14 roster addons it has zero callers. Seven addons do mirror it as a no-op in their degradation stubs. These are stub entries, not callers, and removing the export cannot turn any of them red (see bars).
candidates.bars: library-stack-§7's promotion bars ('A shape MUST clear all three bars before it moves upstream: 1. Two or more consumers, with the same semantics ... 2. No per-consumer escape hatches ... 3. A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code') govern what moves INTO the library. This candidate takes surface out, so they apply in reverse. Bar 1: zero consumers, verified, so the export fails the bar it would need to stay as surface. Bars 2 and 3: not engaged. The bar that does bind is library-stack-§7's 'MUST keep a module's descriptor / API contract additive-only within a major. A field may be added in a later minor, never removed or repurposed'. Three pieces of evidence put a `__` internal outside that contract. (a) docs/api/README.md: 'Kit.publicMembers ... no MAJOR, no MINOR, no MODULES, no `__`-prefixed internals — a stub owes none of those'. (b) LibKa0s/Options.lua:506-509: '`__`-prefixed because it is internal rather than surface: a degradation stub does not mirror it (`Kit.assertSurfaceParity` skips this prefix) ... the library talking to itself across a file boundary'. (c) docs/api/Options/members-29.2.34.2.4.8.1.7.4.2.1.json carries no `__` member. One fact points the other way: the current API document lists it in its member table as 'Test seam' (docs/api/Options/version-29.2.34.2.4.8.1.7.4.2.1-docs.md:1436). That is documentation of an internal, not a consumer-facing contract. No consumer reaches it, so the rationale behind additive-only ('you cannot know who holds what') is answered by measurement.

refutations: Consumer facts hold. LibKa0s/LibKa0s/OptionsTabs.lua:636 is the only definition. :943 and :1036 call the file-local releaseChrome (:619). TABS_MINOR is at :51. A roster-wide grep of all 14 addons, excluding libs/, _kit/ and automated-tests/, finds no caller. Removing a key cannot turn a parity case red. testkit/asserts.lua:274-286 parityProblems iterates the LIVE keys and reports only keys missing from the stub, so a smaller live surface never fails.

Objection to the 'removal is within the rules' argument. library-stack.md:116 says verbatim 'A field may be added in a later minor, never removed or repurposed'. No rule in the standard exempts `__` members. The exemption the analyst builds rests on docs/api/README.md:36 (a parity-assertion note) and a code comment at LibKa0s/Options.lua:506-509. Neither is the standard. The current contract document also lists the member in its member table (docs/api/Options/version-29.2.34.2.4.8.1.7.4.2.1-docs.md:1436, 'Test seam'). The CHANGELOG shows no earlier case of the library removing a documented `__` export, so this would be the first. Seven addons mirroring it is evidence that consumers treated it as surface. The standard sentence the analyst calls optional should be a prerequisite (or ride with the fix in the same release). Without it, the fix breaks a MUST as written.

Payload-weight objection, partial. CHANGELOG.md v1.75.0 (:13-18) currently says 'No payload file under LibKa0s/ has changed'. The icon prune touches media, not Lua. Adding a Lua minor makes v1.75.0 a runtime-code release, which formally owes an in-client smoke. That cost is small but not 'close to zero'. The owner should choose deliberately between folding it in and holding it for the next payload release. The analyst's recommendation is reasonable, but the analyst understates the cost.

analysis.cluster: LibKa0s #46 + #47: the complexity runner misreads a lizard crash (exit status, traceback parsed as footer, invalid manifest, crash shown as blind) and the for/while-header function-literal shape

candidates.name: #46 Runner: treat a lizard crash as a crash. Keep stderr out of the parse, check the footer's shape, make fld numeric, and use the right exit-status rule
candidates.rationale: Confirmed on LibKa0s master (d9f9454, kit revision 40) by running the real runner over a scratch fixture: crash.lua (`for name, fn in pairs({\n  A = function() f() end,\n}) do g(name, fn) end`) plus fine.lua. Console: `complexity fail — str warnings (fun rate instance,), TypeError: NLOC / expected funcs, avg NLOC sequence ...`. It reported `lizard blind in 2 file(s)` (fine.lua included). manifest.json line 16 held `"warnings": str, ... "nloc": TypeError:` and json.load failed with `Expecting value: line 16 column 70`. The cause is that testkit/run-automated-tests.sh:508 runs `raw="$(cd "$CX_TMP/src" && bounded lizard ... . 2>&1)"`: stderr is merged and the exit status is discarded. :522 takes `tail -1` as the footer. :523-531 `fld` passes any token through. :697 interpolates the fields unquoted. The same garbage reaches the console fmt (:638-639), the RESULTS.md trend row (:738) and the watch-list lead (:1061-1064). The suite status itself is already `fail` today, because parity calls every file blind, so the release gate is not falsely passed. The defects are a wrong diagnosis, an unparseable manifest and a polluted trend row. The issue's proposed rule is wrong in one load-bearing place. It says to mark complexity fail with 'lizard exited <rc>' whenever the status is non-zero. lizard 1.24.0 main() (site-packages/lizard.py:1182-1184) returns 1 whenever `0 <= options.number < warning_count`, and the default -i is 0. Measured: a single CCN-17 function gives rc=1 with a perfectly valid footer. A Python traceback also exits 1. rc!=0 therefore cannot mean 'crashed'. The issue's rule would zero every CCN figure and suppress the watch list the moment any addon has a function above 15, which is exactly when the record matters. All 14 roster addons' newest manifests show warnings 0 today, so the regression would be latent until the first warning. performance-§10 fixes the invocation, so adding `-i -1` is not allowed either. Correct rule: a run is valid iff the line two below `^Total nloc` holds 8 numeric fields AND rc is 0 or 1. Anything else (no footer, a non-numeric footer, rc 124/137 from `timeout`, rc 2 from an argument error, a traceback on stderr) is a crash or bound.
candidates.bars: library-stack-§7's three promotion bars ('1. Two or more consumers, with the same semantics', '2. No per-consumer escape hatches', '3. A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code') govern moving a shape upstream. This is a defect in code already upstream: the runner is MUST-vendored by automated-tests-§2 ('MUST run the suites through tests/_kit/run-automated-tests.sh ... byte-identical in every addon'), so all 14 roster addons plus LibKa0s itself consume it with identical semantics by construction. Bar 2: the fix adds no flag. Bar 3: lizard's footer layout and exit contract (print_total at lizard.py:839-853, main at :1182) are what the runner already depends on. The bars are therefore satisfied trivially and are not the operative test. The operative rule is automated-tests-§3: 'A green run that silently measured nothing is worse than a red one, because it is believed', and the manifest must be machine-readable for /dev-copilot:bump-version.

verdicts.name: #46 Runner: treat a lizard crash as a crash (stderr out of raw, anchored numeric footer, numeric fld, exit rule rc in {0,1})
refutations: Re-verified the analyst's central correction, and the issue's rule is wrong as the analyst says. lizard 1.24.0 main() (site-packages/lizard.py:1182-1184: `if 0 <= options.number < warning_count: return 1`) returns 1 on any warned run. I measured it: a CCN-18 fixture under `lizard -l lua -L 1500 .` gave rc=1 with a valid footer and an empty stderr. Issue #46 'If either check fails ... set every CCN_* to zero' would therefore zero the figures and kill the watch list the first time an addon crosses CCN 15. Pinning case (b) is mandatory.

The analyst's list says ':539 (CCN_MAX, safe because it reads only `@` rows)'. That is NOT safe on the crash path. lizard streams function rows file by file before it raises. Measured with a.lua, z.lua and crash.lua: stdout held `z@1-1@./z.lua` and `a@1-1@./a.lua` before the TypeError. On a crash, CCN_MAX is therefore a partial max over whichever files os.walk reached first, in walk order, not sorted. The invalid path must zero or discard CCN_MAX along with the footer fields. Add an assertion to fixture (a): its fake should print one `@` row before the traceback and require maxCcn 0.

Ordering constraint the analyst's change list omits: run-automated-tests.sh:514 does `rm -rf "$CX_TMP"` right after parity. cx_valid, and the per-file retry it hands off to, must run before that line, because the shadow tree and $CX_TMP/files are gone after it. lizard.err must also be read before the rm.

Hardening for cx_valid: treat a `Traceback` line in lizard.err as invalid even when an 8-field footer exists. main() still runs print_extension_results and list(result) after print_total (lizard.py:1176-1177), so a late raise could follow a good footer. It costs nothing and keeps 'raised' from ever being reported as a pass.

Footer anchor confirmed: the values line is exactly two below `^Total nloc` (header, dashes, values). Both the warned and unwarned outputs show it. Kit.VERSION is 40 on master d9f9454 (framework.lua:20), so 41 is right. Roster kits: AbsorbTracker/PGFE 38, DropWatcher/QuickComms 39. QuickComms is on master now. testkit/ and tests/_kit/ runners are byte-identical (cmp).
missed_items: Zero CCN_MAX on an invalid run. It is computed from partial streamed `@` rows and would otherwise go to the manifest and the trend row as a real-looking number.
Do the validity check and any retry before run-automated-tests.sh:514 removes $CX_TMP.
Treat a Traceback on stderr as invalid regardless of the footer.

refutations: The rationale says it 'Verified lizard prints nothing per-file on the crash'. That is half false. The per-file summary table (`NLOC Avg.NLOC ... function_cnt file`, which S.listedCounts at lizard_sighted.lua:162-178 reads) is indeed absent, so the 'every file blind' diagnosis holds. But the function rows do stream before the raise (measured: z.lua and a.lua rows printed, then the TypeError). Attribution from the stream is still unreliable, because walk order is unsorted and function-less files print nothing. The per-file retry is still the right attribution method, but the claim should be corrected.

The 'measure the rest' re-run is the part with the thinnest justification, and it is a new behaviour, not a defect fix. It needs a second whole-tree lizard invocation path, mutation of the shadow and of $CX_TMP/files, a second cx_valid, and a 'whole tree' fallback. All of that serves a run whose status is already fail and blocks the release. The only remedy is a source hoist, after which the next run measures everything. The figures it produces are over a subset, and they enter the RESULTS.md trend row, which the analyst flags as a risk. That is extra branching in a 1234-line MUST-vendored file for a shape seen once in the collection's history (PGFE RegionTags.lua, hoisted in 10350bc) and zero times today. The issue's simpler design (name the file, zero the figures, skip parity) covers the actual need.

The zeros objection ('36 -> 0') has a cheaper answer than re-measuring. On a crashed run, the RESULTS.md trend row and the console can print the CCN columns as 'n/a (lizard raised)'. The manifest stays numeric (0) under the existing schema, and status=fail tells readers not to trust them. No figures over a subset ever enter the trend.

Per-file retry: keep it. Naming the file is the real value, and the issue asks for it. Skipping it on 124/137 is correct. It must run inside the shadow before :514's rm, with the same flags (`-l lua -L 1500`), so the reported paths and lines are the real files'.

test_kit_runner.lua:333-354 already pins the single-line silent drop `for _, p in ipairs({ function() return 1 end }) do p() end` as blind. That case must keep passing unchanged, which shows blind and crashed really are distinct buckets.
missed_items: Correct the 'prints nothing per-file' claim in version-41 docs. Function rows stream; only the per-file table is missing.
On the crash path, render the trend-row CCN columns as n/a rather than 0, whichever re-measure option the owner picks.
scope_cuts: Cut 'remove crashed files from the shadow and re-run the fixed command over the rest'. On a crash, name the crashed file(s) via the per-file retry, set the figures to 0 in the manifest and n/a in RESULTS.md/console, skip parity, and set status fail. This also drops fixture (e)'s 'fine.lua measured (functions=1)' assertion, which becomes 'fine.lua is not reported blind', and removes the whole-tree-fallback branch (f), which stays only as 'no single file reproduces'.

Keep crashedFiles as an additive manifest field (schema stays 1). It is cheap and gives bump-version a precise reason. Do not add more fields, such as per-file exception text in the manifest. The text belongs in complexity.txt and the note.

verdicts.name: #47 optional detector S.forInFunctionLiterals(src)
refutations: Agree. library-stack.md:228 bar 1, 'Two or more consumers, with the same semantics', fails: there are zero current instances and the one historic one is already hoisted in source. Bar 3 at :235, 'A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code ... whether that change is plausible this year', also fails, because the detector encodes one lizard release's reader bug. The issue's own repro, `for name, fn in pairs({ A = function() end }) do end` on one line, does not crash 1.24.0. My crash needed the multi-line keyed form (`for name, fn in pairs({\n  A = function() f() end,\n}) do ... end` gave rc=1 with TypeError). So a detector built from the issue's description would target the wrong shape. Record the rejection per library-stack.md:259 ('SHOULD record a rejection with its reason where the next author will look').
scope_cuts: The static hint in the crashed note should stay to one sentence, and it should be worded as 'known lizard 1.24.0 trigger', not as a rule, so a future lizard change does not make it misleading.

verdicts.name: #47 implied: neutralise the shape in the sighted shadow
refutations: Agree. The shadow's contract is that only reader hazards change and every figure stays the real file's. A rewrite that removes a `for` decision point under-counts CCN, which is the unsafe direction for a ceiling. Hoisting in source is the remedy the standard already prescribes. I did not re-measure the `fo_` rename CCN delta myself. The claim that lizard counts `for` as a decision point is consistent with its CCN model, and the rejection holds even without it, because one historic instance does not justify changing the shadow.

verdicts.name: Standard and plugin ripple: hazard row, crashed bucket, release gate, playbook, #92, dev-copilot readers
refutations: The release-gate wording change ('blindFiles at 0 and crashedFiles at 0') is redundant. A crashed run already has complexity status fail, and the gate already requires 'complexity pass'. Adding a second term creates two sources of truth that can drift. It is better to state in §3 that a raised or bounded lizard run is complexity not passing. That is a clarification, and arguably not even a new MUST, because §3 already says an unmeasured claim is not a pass. If it is a clarification, a patch bump is enough. Do not mint v2.86.0 for a new MUST that the existing text already implies.

The hazard-row correction is right and needed. My measurements agree: the single-line form at file scope is dropped and not raised, and the multi-line keyed header table raises TypeError. That closes WowAddonStandards#8 with corrected facts.

The dev-copilot bump-version Sighted row change can wait or be skipped. The gate refuses on status already, as the analyst's own risk note says. Printing crashedFiles is cosmetic, so it should ride the next dev-copilot release and not be a coordinated dependency.
missed_items: The playbook text should say that function rows can appear before the traceback in complexity.txt, so that a reader of a crashed bundle does not take the partial rows as a measurement.
scope_cuts: Drop the release-gate term change. Keep 'complexity pass'.
Prefer a clarification (patch bump) over a new MUST with a minor bump, unless the owner wants crashedFiles to be normative.
Only touch the anti-patterns #92 wording if the other edits are already being made in that file. It is optional.
Make the dev-copilot reader updates opportunistic rather than a blocking dependency.

owner_questions: When lizard raises on a file, the runner can show the CCN columns as n/a in RESULTS.md and the console. The manifest would hold 0, the file would be named, and status would be fail. The alternative is the analyst's re-measure of the remaining files, which adds a second lizard path and puts figures for only part of the tree into the trend row. The challenger recommends n/a.

Is 'a raised or bounded lizard run is not a complexity pass' a clarification of automated-tests-§3, which would be a patch bump, or a new MUST with crashedFiles named normatively, which would be v2.86.0?
Should kit revision 41 (#46 + #47, plus #45's seam removal if accepted) ship inside the unreleased v1.75.0, or should it be cut as v1.76.0?

analysis.cluster: LibKa0s#48: a shared test-mode strip widget, lifted from DropWatcher's buildBanner

candidates.name: W.TestStrip(parent, opts): the DropWatcher test-mode strip promoted into LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0
candidates.rationale: Only one addon draws a strip today. It is DropWatcher, and its copy is no longer the simple widget the issue describes: it carries a compact-layout variant that is tied into DropWatcher's own chrome. The other window addons that mark test mode do it another way: a red title badge in LootHistory and BankLedger, an inline title colour in MultiMeters, a green marker on the drag strip and the dial hub in QuickComms, and sample content in WhatGroup. Adopting the strip there would be a redesign, not a lift of a copy that already exists, so the promotion would create its own consumers. The thing being shared is about 18 lines of frame, texture and font-string layout with almost no semantic content. Positioning and the body shift stay in each host either way (the issue says so itself), so the library would save each adopter very little. The Widgets 'two skins to keep in step' argument does apply, but only once a second copy actually exists. Keep it in DropWatcher. Record the rejection in docs/api/CONSUMERS.md (or the Widgets header's 'WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT' block) and re-check when a second window really ships a strip.
candidates.bars:
Bars quoted from WowAddonStandards/standards/standards/library-stack.md §7 ('What earns promotion', lines ~221-235 of the file).
(1) "Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape." FAILS. Exactly one consumer is verified: DropWatcher/modules/Window.lua:434-452 (buildBanner) plus CompactChrome.lua:365-377 (layoutStrip), :452-456 and :473-482 (CC.BannerH). LootHistory/modules/Browser.lua:886-891 and BankLedger/modules/Browser.lua:992-997 draw a different thing: a GameFontNormalLarge red 'TEST MODE' font string to the right of the title, with no strip, icon, fill or tooltip. MultiMeters/modules/Window_Header.lua:340-342 appends '|cffff2020TEST MODE|r' to the title, and :1193 adds 'Test' to the session line. QuickComms/modules/Pad_Render.lua:527-536 (R.StripLabel, green marker on the pad's drag strip) and modules/Dial.lua:199 (hub label) draw on pads and a dial, not on a window with a filter bar. WhatGroup has no marker on the popup: its sample title reads 'Test Group — Windrunner Spire +12' (core/WhatGroup.lua:1294), and a chat line is printed (modules/Frame.lua:1128). None of these would be a strip consumer without a redesign first.
(2) "No per-consumer escape hatches... a flag that changes what the function does is the tell." AT RISK. The issue's API (text, tooltip, icon, SetShown, SetText) cannot carry DropWatcher's real behaviour. That behaviour switches between full and compact text, turns word-wrap on in compact (CompactChrome.lua:368-376), and measures a one- or two-line height through GetUnboundedStringWidth against the room it has (CompactChrome.lua:473-482). Even the source consumer would need wrap and measure options. One of those is presentation, but the height contract leaks into every host's body layout (Window.lua:480).
(3) "A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code." WEAK. The strip has already changed shape once since the issue was filed: the compact variant was added, and the text changed from 'placeholder drops' to 'sample drops of real items'. Its colour comes from an addon-local tone (C.TONE.warn, DropWatcher core/Constants.lua:149), and the art has to arrive as a resolved path because Widgets cannot call Media (Widgets.lua:12-17). A restyle in any one addon makes the shared version wrong, and the owner has restyled DropWatcher's chrome in most feedback rounds this month.
Rule "MUST NOT promote on frequency alone. High frequency plus low semantic content..." The frequency here is low (one) and the semantic content is low too, which argues even more strongly against promotion.
verified_consumers: DropWatcher/modules/Window.lua:433-452 buildBanner: the only real consumer. 22px (K.BANNER_H, core/Constants.lua:62, drawn at H-4), anchored under f.filterHost, fill C.TONE.warn at alpha 0.12, 12px NS.Icon('info'), GameFontNormalSmall text, tooltip NS.WindowTitleBar.TestTip (modules/WindowTitleBar.lua:144-150) through Window.AttachTooltip (Window.lua:248); shown at Window.lua:626; body shifted at Window.lua:480
DropWatcher/modules/CompactChrome.lua:365-377, 452-456, 473-482: compact text, word-wrap, and measured one- or two-line height. This is part of the strip today and is not in the issue's API
LootHistory/modules/Browser.lua:580-584, 885-891: a red 'TEST MODE' title badge, not a strip. NOT the same semantics or shape; adopting the strip would be a redesign
BankLedger/modules/Browser.lua:741-742, 991-997: the same red title badge as LootHistory, byte-identical code. NOT a strip consumer

MultiMeters/modules/Window_Header.lua:340-344, 1193: a red 'TEST MODE' inside the title text, plus 'Test' on the session line. A meter window has no filter bar, and the code comment there argues the title is the deliberate place for it. FALSE consumer

QuickComms/modules/Pad_Render.lua:527-536, Pad.lua:350, Dial.lua:199: a green PREVIEW or TEST MODE marker on the pad's drag strip and the dial hub. These are not windows with a filter bar and the roster does not name them as adopters. Not a consumer (QuickComms read on master)
WhatGroup/modules/Frame.lua:1124-1128, core/WhatGroup.lua:1293-1295: sample content plus a chat line; no on-popup marker. Correctly excluded from the strip
AuraMaster: modules/Anchors.lua:835 and core/Constants.lua:216 put a TEST tag on each container's drag handle. There is no window; correctly excluded
libka0s_changes: None now.

Record the rejection with its re-check trigger in LibKa0s docs/api/CONSUMERS.md, or in the 'WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT' comment block in LibKa0s/Widgets.lua (§7 'SHOULD record a rejection... where the next author will look'). That is a doc or comment-only change with no minor bump. Close #48 as deferred and link the re-check trigger.

If it is re-opened and accepted later: add LibKa0s/WidgetsNotice.lua (or extend Widgets.lua) as additive Widgets-1.0 minor 13 (current MINOR is 12, Widgets.lua:36), list it in LibKa0s.xml and tests/majors.lua, add docs/api/Widgets/version-13-docs.md and members-13.json through tools/gen-api-members.lua, a headless test for build, SetShown, SetText and the measured height, and a CHANGELOG entry under the then-unreleased version. No Kit.VERSION change is needed unless the mock gains GetUnboundedStringWidth (framework.lua Kit.VERSION is 40 today).
standard_changes: See the separate standard-only candidate. No library-stack change for this one beyond optionally naming it as a recorded rejection, beside the schema-migration example, if the owner wants a second worked example.
addon_adoptions: None. DropWatcher keeps buildBanner and CompactChrome's strip code as they are.

Re-check trigger: when a second window addon actually ships a strip between its filter bar and its body (most likely LootHistory or BankLedger, if the owner chooses to replace the title badge), compare the two copies, and promote only if both use the same anchor contract, the same tone and the same height rule without per-addon flags.
candidates.api_sketch: Deferred. If re-opened: W.Notice(parent, { text, tooltip = fn|string, icon = resolvedPath|nil, tone = {r,g,b} }) -> strip with :SetText(s), :SetShown(b) and :Height(wrap) -> number. The caller anchors it and shifts its body by :Height(). The tone is passed in, never looked up, because LibKa0s has no tone table. Named generically rather than 'TestStrip' because it carries no test-mode logic.

risks: Promoting now would freeze an API that DropWatcher itself cannot adopt without wrap and height options, so the library would gain surface that even the source addon does not use (additive-only, kept forever).

false_or_stale_claims: 'DropWatcher/modules/Window.lua, buildBanner draws it today ... placeholder drops in every state' is STALE: the text is now 'sample drops of real items in every state' (Window.lua:448), and the strip has a compact variant with wrap and measured height in modules/CompactChrome.lua:365-377 and 473-482, which the proposed API leaves out.

'WhatGroup's test-mode popup ... already says it is showing sample data': only partly true. The popup shows sample content titled 'Test Group — ...' (core/WhatGroup.lua:1294), and the 'sample group info' wording is in a chat line (Frame.lua:1128), not on the popup.
The issue does not mention QuickComms, which also has test mode and a 'Show window' launcher entry (ADDONS.md). It marks test mode on its pads and dial instead.

candidates.name: A shared LibKa0s tone/colour table (the 'shared tone table' the issue assumes exists)
candidates.rationale: The issue takes for granted a shared tone table that does not exist. Creating one would be a separate and much larger promotion. DropWatcher's C.TONE is semantic to its drop tables: good means an upgrade, bad means not wanted, warn means a trade window ending soon (core/Constants.lua:143-160). Other addons give the same names other meanings or hard-code their colours: LootHistory and BankLedger use 1, 0.15, 0.15 red, and MultiMeters uses ff2020. No second consumer with the same semantics has been shown.
candidates.bars: (1) "Two or more consumers, with the same semantics": none shown. DropWatcher's tones are domain verdicts, and the other addons' test-mode reds are a different colour with a different meaning (alarm, not warn). (3) "A stable abstraction": palette choices are the most restyled thing in the collection. Rule "MUST NOT promote a shape whose consumers disagree": the consumers disagree on presentation, which is allowed, but there is nothing here to share.

LootHistory/modules/Browser.lua:890 and BankLedger/modules/Browser.lua:995: SetTextColor(1, 0.15, 0.15). This is a hard-coded red, not a tone
MultiMeters/modules/Window_Header.lua:341: '|cffff2020' inline red

standard_changes: None.

challenge.cluster: LibKa0s#48: shared test-mode strip widget (from DropWatcher buildBanner)

verdicts.name: W.TestStrip(parent, opts): DropWatcher test-mode strip into LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0
refutations: Re-verified that there is exactly one strip consumer. DropWatcher/modules/Window.lua:433-452 (buildBanner) holds a fill in C.TONE.warn at 0.12, NS.Icon('info'), GameFontNormalSmall text and Window.AttachTooltip(b, NS.WindowTitleBar.TestTip). layoutPanes at Window.lua:480 shifts the body by NS.CompactChrome.BannerH(). So bar 1 of library-stack.md section 7 fails: 'Two or more consumers, with the same semantics, not merely the same shape.'

The strip has already diverged from the API the issue proposes. CompactChrome.lua:365-377 (layoutStrip) swaps the text for a compact string and toggles SetWordWrap(compact). CompactChrome.lua:473-482 (CC.BannerH) measures GetUnboundedStringWidth against the available room to choose a one- or two-line height. The source consumer would therefore need wrap and measure options. That is bar 2's tell: 'a flag that changes what the function does'. The height feeds the host's body layout, so it is a contract and not just presentation.

Named adopters re-verified as false consumers. LootHistory/modules/Browser.lua:887-892 and BankLedger/modules/Browser.lua:992-997 are byte-identical red GameFontNormalLarge 'TEST MODE' title badges (SetTextColor(1,0.15,0.15)). MultiMeters/modules/Window_Header.lua:340-341 puts the marker inline in the title, and the comment at :328-333 argues deliberately for title placement. None of them draws a strip, so adoption would be a redesign that the promotion itself creates.

'take its colors from the shared tone table' is false: there are no TONE hits in LibKa0s/LibKa0s/*.lua. Widgets.lua:36 is MINOR 12, and Widgets cannot resolve Media icons, so the host would pass in both the colour and the art. Once those are passed in, the shared code is roughly 15 lines of CreateTexture/CreateFontString/SetPoint. Section 7 calls this 'High frequency plus low semantic content' at a frequency of one.

Minor citation slip in the analyst's QuickComms evidence. Dial.lua:199 only builds plan.testText. The hub label is drawn in modules/Dial_Render.lua:358 onward. Pad.lua:350 and Pad_Render.lua:527 are correct. QuickComms is confirmed on master with a clean tree. The conclusion is unchanged.
scope_cuts: Do not pre-design W.Notice or :Height(wrap) in the deferral record. An API sketch in CONSUMERS.md anchors the next author to a shape that has no second consumer yet. Record only the rejection, the bar that failed and the re-check trigger.

Do not count the owner question 'should LH/BL switch to a strip?' as an argument for promotion. If the owner says yes, build the strip in LH or BL first, then compare it with DropWatcher's copy, including the compact/wrap behaviour, before reopening.
missed_items: The re-check trigger should require the second copy to match the compact-layout height rule as well, or to deliberately not need it. Otherwise a second copy without compact mode will look like 'same shape' and pass a shallow comparison.

Where the rejection is recorded: the 'WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT' block is at LibKa0s/LibKa0s/Widgets.lua:23, and docs/api/CONSUMERS.md exists. Choose one and do not write it in both places, or the two copies will drift.

verdicts.name: Shared LibKa0s tone/colour table
refutations: Confirmed that no TONE exists in the LibKa0s payload. DropWatcher's C.TONE is domain-semantic. The other test-mode markers use hard-coded reds: LootHistory/BankLedger Browser.lua SetTextColor(1,0.15,0.15), MultiMeters Window_Header.lua:341 |cffff2020, and AuraMaster's orange TEST tag (core/Constants.lua:214-216). QuickComms uses green (Pad_Render.lua:527). Four colours across five addons is a disagreement on presentation with no shared semantics, so bar 1 fails.

verdicts.name: Standard: a test mode MUST visibly mark every display it draws (preview-mode), with the strip as the recommended form for a filter-bar window (standalone-windows)
refutations: The gap is confirmed. WowAddonStandards/standards/standards/preview-mode.md (14 lines) requires placeholder data, the switch and how test mode ends, but never requires the display to say it is showing test data.

The census of affected addons is incomplete. AbsorbTracker (modules/Display.lua:55, 310), KickCD (settings/General.lua:22), PanelMaster (settings/Schema.lua:608) and PartyFrameEnhanced (modules/StandIn.lua:8) all use preview-mode.md:10's exception, where unlocking is the preview. The proposed bullet says 'a test mode MUST mark every display' and does not say whether the unlock-preview counts. candidates.name: #49 item 1: chat sender (Compat.ChatSender) into LibKa0s-Compat-1.0's reader arm
candidates.rationale: The issue says this clears all three bars. Bar 1 is met in the letter: two production consumers with the same resolution order. Promoting it still buys nothing and costs surface. The member is one presence guard (`C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage`, else the global). On every admitted client the fallback rung cannot be reached: both TOCs say `## Interface: 120105`, and both copies' own comments say the namespaced member has existed since 11.2.0 (MultiMeters core/Compat.lua:754-756). That leaves no content, the same shape as the `C_StringUtil.CreateNumericRuleFormatter` presence guard that LibKa0s already rejects in docs/api/Compat/version-1-docs.md, 'Two consumers, but no content' (line ~276). Adopting it also deletes nothing from either host. Drop Watcher must keep `NS.Compat.ChatSender` as a seam, because core/SimSeam.lua:76 wraps it as a GUARDED member so a simulation never whispers. MultiMeters' tests swap it (tests/test_export.lua:1057-1078). Each host would also gain a reader-arm stub (`function() return nil end`) and the degraded-load test the Compat adoption section requires. Library-stack-§7 says it MUST NOT promote on frequency alone, and 'high frequency plus low semantic content' is exactly this case at a frequency of two. Addon-sent chat policy (one send per click, the 255-byte limit, the restriction queue, never SAY/YELL) is real shared content, but it belongs in the standard (WowAddonStandards#11), not in a resolver.

candidates.rationale: One consumer. Drop Watcher calls ReadTooltipLine from four of its own members (core/Compat.lua:158, :175, :209, :679), all in-addon. ConsumableMaster's `TooltipCache.Get` (core/TooltipCache.lua:439-450, parseLines) collects several facts per tooltip across all lines (stat buffs, heal amounts, the longest duration). It is not a first-answer read, and it uses no line types. For durations, CM parses English literal 'N hour/min/sec' fragments inside effect sentences and keeps the largest. DW decodes a whole localized duration sentence from the client's GlobalStrings. These are different questions. Both do hit the same 12.x quirk, where C_TooltipInfo returns raw `|4singular:plural;` grammar (CM core/TooltipCache.lua:126-140; DW commit 384c398, TextParse.ExpandPlural). LootHistory ScanBound needs the readable/retrieving distinction and whole-line wording matches. CM TooltipCache gathers many facts across every line. Their duration parsing answers a different question (an English fragment inside an effect line, largest unit wins, versus a whole localized sentence). Bar 2: an adopter would need flags, for example 'report readable', 'aggregate rather than first', or 'English literals'. Those are the consumers' divergence written as configuration. FAILS. Bar 3: the duration decoder needed a fix within a week of shipping (12.1.5's unexpanded `|4hour:hrs;`, DW 384c398), and Enum.TooltipDataLineType coverage changes with patches. NOT stable this year.

candidates.name: #49 item 3 / #51 item 2: loot-line parser (DropWatcher modules/LootParser.lua vs LootHistory core/Util.lua ParseSelfLoot)
candidates.rationale: #51 says 'one every-looter parser with a self-only filter would serve both'. That is false: the two parsers disagree about correctness on the same lines, not just about scope. LootHistory treats crafting and refund lines as receipts with a source tag (core/Util.lua:160-175: LOOT_ITEM_CREATED_SELF[_MULTIPLE] → source CRAFT, LOOT_ITEM_REFUND[_MULTIPLE] → REFUND). Drop Watcher rejects crafting lines as not-a-drop (modules/LootParser.lua:63-67: reject CHANGED_OWN_ITEM, LOOT_ITEM_CREATED_SELF*, CREATED_ITEM*) and has no refund shape. Their outputs differ too. LH returns (link, qty, sourceTag), feeds a separate roll-won parser (Util.ParseRollWon) and has currency and money siblings. DW returns {looterName, looterGUID, link, qty, kind, isSelf}, resolves looters through its roster, and counts secrets. A shared parser would need a 'which lines are receipts' flag and an output adapter per consumer, which is bar 2's tell. Library-stack-§7 also says MUST NOT promote a shape whose consumers disagree about correctness. What the two do share is the idea of rebuilding when another addon (PrettyChat) rewrites the globals, compared with rawequal. That is a technique, and each copy is about ten lines.
candidates.bars: Bar 1, verbatim: 'Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape.' NOT MET: self-only versus every looter, and opposite answers on crafted lines. Bar 2, verbatim: 'If adopting it requires a behavior flag per consumer, those flags are the consumers' divergence re-encoded as configuration.' FAILS: it would need a receipt-set flag (craft/refund in or out), a looter-scope flag and an output-shape adapter. Bar 3: the LOOT_ITEM* grammar is stable, but the policy over it is not shared. Additional MUST NOT, verbatim: 'MUST NOT promote a shape whose consumers disagree about correctness, as opposed to presentation.' Triggered by the crafted-line disagreement.

LootHistory core/Util.lua:200 (Util.ParseSelfLoot), called from modules/Collector.lua:165: self only; ACCEPTS crafted and refund lines with source tags (:160-175); no positional handling (toLootPattern :109); English-only addon (locales/enUS.lua only).

verdicts.name: LootHistory Price-sources host has no OnRelease undo (options-ui-§19)
refutations: The defect is real against the letter of the rule. LootHistory settings/Panel.lua:792-805 runs AceGUI:Create('SimpleGroup'), then hf:SetParent(placeholder.frame), with no SetCallback('OnRelease'). The only undo is renderer-side, at :997-1004. options-ui.md:471 reads: 'The undo MUST live in that widget's own single "OnRelease". A renderer-side park ... does not satisfy this rule'. The placeholder is created by the addon, so setting OnRelease on it does not break the one-callback rule (:473).

Severity is overstated if this is filed as medium. It should be low, because the failure is latent today. LH draws its General strip by hand (Panel.lua:946-950), so a tab click re-enters renderGeneral (O.SetRenderer at :1090; the comment at :927 says the strip's onSelect re-enters the page renderer). The test at tests/test_panel.lua:681-688 pins the park on tab switch. The placeholder is a direct scroll child, so no parent ReleaseChildren reaches it, and every ClearScroll of that scroll goes through renderGeneral. The bug only shows if a release path the renderer does not see is added later. It is still a MUST violation with no deviation row, so it should be fixed.

The proposed fix and test are feasible. The vendored mock fires OnRelease on release (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:1389), so the characterization test (release the placeholder outside renderGeneral, then assert _priHost is parented to ctx.panel and hidden) can go red before the fix. candidates.name: Item.BonusIDsFromLink(link): the ordered bonus ids of an item link or bare item string (the issue missed this one)
candidates.rationale: This is the only part of the item read that has two or more real consumers with the same semantics, and the issue did not name them. Bank Ledger (core/Util.lua WowheadURL) and Loot History (modules/Export.lua WowheadLink) each wrote the same positional walk: split the item string keeping empty fields, read field 13 as the bonus count, then collect fields 14..13+n as numbers. Drop Watcher's LinkDetail does the same walk at core/ItemRead.lua:45-58. The function carries real domain knowledge that can be got wrong, namely field 13 and keeping empty fields (BL's comment at Util.lua:99-100 records that trap). It holds no policy and calls no client API, so it has no secret, cache or simulator-seam questions. It sits naturally beside ItemIDFromLink and QualityFromLink as a fifth link primitive. Ship only this one primitive. Each Wowhead URL builder stays in its addon.
candidates.bars: Bar 1, "Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape": PASS. BL core/Util.lua:101-105 + 118-122 and LH modules/Export.lua:29 + 46-55 both produce the bonus ids in link order, stop at the declared count and skip empty fields (BL with tonumber, LH with ~= "", which gives the same result because LH's capture pattern [%-%d:]+ admits only digits). DW core/ItemRead.lua:55-58 is a third copy of the same walk inside LinkDetail. Bar 2, "No per-consumer escape hatches ... a flag that changes what the function does is the tell": PASS. The function takes no argument besides the link. Bar 3, "A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code. Ask what would have to change for the shared version to be wrong": PASS. It would be wrong only if Blizzard moved the bonus count off field 13 of the item string. That layout has been stable for years, and if it ever moves, all three copies break together, so one fix upstream beats three. "MUST NOT promote on frequency alone. High frequency plus low semantic content": not triggered, because there are three sites (not hundreds) and the content is positional knowledge, not a guard. "MUST NOT promote a shape whose consumers disagree about correctness": no disagreement exists. Caveat for the owner's high bar: two of the three uses feed a Wowhead URL, which is presentation, and DW would probably keep its own walk because LinkDetail also needs the modifier offset after the bonus list. So the realistic adoption is BL and LH (two consumers), which still clears bar 1.

That is latent and does not occur in real links.

No other roster addon parses bonus ids. I grepped all 14 for item-string field walks, numBonus, bonusID and GetDetailedItemLevelInfo/GetCurrentItemLevel. ConsumableMaster only builds item:<id> macro strings, PrettyChat matches only GlobalStrings text, and the rest have no hits.

candidates.api_sketch:
--- The bonus ids an item link (or bare item string) carries, in link order. {} for an item with none; nil for a string that holds no item.
function lib.BonusIDsFromLink(link)
  if type(link) ~= "string" then return nil end
  local s = link:match("item:([%-%d:]*)")
  if not s then return nil end
  local f = {}
  for v in (s .. ":"):gmatch("([^:]*):") do f[#f + 1] = v end
  if not tonumber(f[1]) then return nil end
  local out = {}
  for i = 14, 13 + (tonumber(f[13]) or 0) do
    local id = tonumber(f[i]); if id then out[#out + 1] = id end
  end
  return out
end
risks: Additive-only surface kept forever. The function is small and policy-free, so the risk is low.

Secret strings: like ItemIDFromLink, it does not guard against a secret link. Callers pass stored or plain links, and DW's NS.Compat already strips secrets. Adding a guard would need IsSecret from LibKa0s-Compat, which is a fourth inter-module edge that the standard's 'exactly three second edges' text would have to absorb. Keep parity with ItemIDFromLink instead.
Realistic adoption is two (BL, LH), and both are Wowhead-URL presentation code. If the owner reads bar 1 as 'two consumers of a non-presentation need', this drops to defer.

verdicts.name: Item.BonusIDsFromLink(link)
refutations: The consumer facts check out but argue against shipping. BankLedger core/Util.lua:101-105 and :118-122, and LootHistory modules/Export.lua:29 and :45-55, are the only two copies. Each has exactly one call site, and both feed a Wowhead URL: BL modules/Export.lua:57 calls NS.Util.WowheadURL and LH modules/Export.lua:116 calls E:WowheadLink. I grepped all roster addons for bonus id, numBonus, [13], F_BONUS_COUNT and wowhead outside libs/ and tests/_kit/. That found no other bonus-id consumer. QuickComms only links wowhead.com/icons (settings/IconBrowser.lua:82), and the [13] hits in ConsumableMaster, MultiMeters and LootHistory BrowserTable are unrelated tables.

The analyst is inconsistent. They reject the Wowhead URL builder as presentation, yet the bonus walk has no consumer except that same URL builder in the same two addons. If the URL is presentation that stays per addon, the walk's whole demand is presentation too. That makes it a helper split out of a rejected candidate, not a separately demanded primitive.

Adopting does not remove the duplication; it adds a copy. Both addons wire Item through a library-absent stub that re-implements every primitive locally: BankLedger core/ItemSetup.lua:21-24 says 'The same four primitives, locally', and the stub table starts at :36. LootHistory core/ItemSetup.lua:41-67 does the same. The analyst's own adoption plan adds BonusIDsFromLink to both stubs plus stub-parity tests. The walk would then exist in the library, in two stubs and in DW's LinkDetail: four copies instead of three, with additive-only library surface forever. Bar 1 is met on paper, but the promotion consolidates nothing.

No defect or divergence drives this. Both copies are already pinned by characterization tests (BankLedger tests/test_util.lua:144-173, LootHistory tests/test_export.lua:15-21), and neither has a recorded bug. Nobody nominated the function: issue #51 item 1 does not mention it, so accepting it widens the issue's scope instead of answering it.

The API sketch does not have the same semantics as the BL copy on odd input. It captures with item:([%-%d:]*), which stops at the first character that is not a digit, '-' or ':'. BL's |Hitem:([^|]+) keeps going and skips non-numeric fields with tonumber, so on a malformed field the two return different bonus lists. Adopting it would change BL's behavior without anyone noticing. Real links never hit this, but it undercuts the analyst's 'same semantics' claim for the exact sketch proposed.
scope_cuts: Do not bump Item to minor 3 and do not add BonusIDsFromLink.
Do not add the stub entries or stub-parity tests in BL or LH, and leave library-stack-§7's Item row and the standard version alone.

Record a rejection with a trigger in the Item API document's 'What this major is not', as library-stack-§7 says ('SHOULD record a rejection with its reason where the next author will look'). The trigger: a consumer of bonus ids that is not a URL builder (for example DW adopting it for identity or modifiers, or BL/LH keying rows by variant), or the two copies diverging or one of them getting a bonus-walk bug.
missed_items: The analyst noted DropWatcher's latent hole and should have filed it as an addon-local fix. At core/ItemRead.lua:55-57, bonus[i] = int(...) can leave a nil hole, and `at = at + #bonus` then takes the modifier offset from a border that Lua leaves undefined, when it should use the declared count in f[F_BONUS_COUNT] (F_BONUS_COUNT = 13, line 32). Real links do not trigger it, but the fix is one line in DW (advance `at` by the declared count) plus a test in tests/test_item_read.lua. It is not a library item.

verdicts.name: LinkDetail + BetterLink
missed_items: DropWatcher docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:299 should say exactly which claim was false: 'Bank Ledger resolves items too, so the read has three would-be adopters'. I confirmed that BL reads no item level and merges no links.

verdicts.name: IdentityKey / SameItem
EffectiveItemLevel (gear level read) vs LootHistory GetItemExtras / GearItemLevel

LH core/Compat.lua:334-339 and :524-533 return nil for non-gear and gate on GetItemInfoInstant, while DW core/ItemRead.lua:122-124 and :152-153 gate on the cached NS.Compat.GetItemInfo. One more divergence the analyst missed: EffectiveItemLevel also accepts a {bag, slot} table (ItemRead.lua:151), which is a location read that LH has no equivalent of. That is a second input type a shared signature would have to carry.

verdicts.name: ItemLevelAt / QualityAt
missed_items: Confirmed: DropWatcher modules/SimWorld.lua:458-462 provides BagItemLevelQuality for simulated items, so a library read that calls C_Item directly would break DW's simulator. Bar 2 fails even with one consumer.

missed_items: The shapes are not quite the same either. DW IR.QualityOf (core/ItemRead.lua:168-174) returns a (quality, source) pair and reads through NS.Compat.GetItemInfo (secret stripping and the sim seam). LH folds the fallback into Compat.GetItemInfo (core/Compat.lua:160-173), where it sits beside a bracket-name fallback and returns no source. BL's refusal (modules/Ledger.lua:310-326, F-006) is the documented correctness disagreement, which LibKa0s Item.lua:1-17 already records.

verdicts.name: Wowhead item URL builder
refutations: The rejection is right, but its consequence applies to candidate 1. Rejecting the URL as presentation also removes the only demand for the bonus walk, so the two candidates should be recorded together under a single trigger.

owner_questions: Do you accept that nothing from #51 item 1 ships? The challenger recommends deferring BonusIDsFromLink: both copies serve only a Wowhead URL, and the stub convention in each addon's core/ItemSetup.lua would keep a local copy anyway, so promoting it adds a copy instead of removing one.

candidates.name: W.SearchBox(parent, width, opts): flat filter-bar search box in the dropdown's skin
candidates.rationale: Three verified window filter bars (LootHistory, BankLedger, DropWatcher) hand-build the same EditBox: BackdropTemplate, a 1px WHITE8X8 line, fill 0.1,0.1,0.12,0.9, line 0.24,0.24,0.27,0.9, height 20, GameFontHighlightSmall, a GameFontDisableSmall hint shown only while the box is empty, and Escape/Enter calling ClearFocus. Two of them compose with W.Autocomplete. The issue named two copies; the third, BankLedger's, is the one Widgets.Dropdown itself was lifted from. Those values are the dropdown's own literals at Widgets.lua:296-299, and WidgetsAutocomplete.lua:68 already copies them as its BORDER/BG. Widgets.lua's header gives the reason the dropdown was promoted: 'Two copies of a widget is two skins to keep in step'. Three copies of the box plus the library's own copies is that problem today. What differs between the copies is either presentation (BankLedger's magnifier mark, DropWatcher's gold focus line) or what the host does with the text (immediate filter, debounced filter, state write plus a debug line on focus loss). The text handling goes through one host callback and HookScript, not through flags. Accept it minimally: one constructor, no setters, no new skin export.
candidates.bars:
Bar 1, 'Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape': CLEARED with three. Each is a live-filter search box on a standalone window's filter bar: typing filters, Enter and Escape only drop focus, empty text shows the hint. LootHistory BrowserFilterBar.lua:404-425, BankLedger Browser.lua:829-852 and DropWatcher WindowFilterBar.lua:686-713 all set identical skin values, font, hint font and focus-drop scripts. Excluded because the semantics differ: MultiMeters Export_Modal.lua:766-807 (captioned name field, skinColor-themed, Enter commits a value) and DropWatcher DetailCard.lua:647 (multiline chat editor).
Bar 2, 'No per-consumer escape hatches... One optional presentation argument is fine; a flag that changes what the function does is the tell': CLEARED. opts.hint is content and opts.icon (a resolved path, BankLedger's magnifier) is presentation. opts.onChange is the host's own action, not a behavior switch. DropWatcher's focus-lost debug line and its `syncing` guard stay host-side, through HookScript and inside its callback. The one per-consumer difference that is not presentation-optional is the gold focus line, and the library makes that call once for everyone: every box wears it, so it is not a flag.
Bar 3, 'A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code. Ask what would have to change for the shared version to be wrong, and whether that change is plausible this year': CLEARED. It would be wrong if a host needed Enter to commit, or a non-live search. That host is a different widget, as MultiMeters' whisper box shows, so it would not be shared anyway. The plausible change this year is a restyle of the flat skin, and that argues for sharing. Anti-frequency rule ('High frequency plus low semantic content'): this is not an inline idiom like the optional-object guard. It is a skinned control whose risk is visual drift beside W.Dropdown, the same argument the dropdown and copy window were promoted on. Correctness disagreement: none, because the filtering logic stays with the host.

candidates.api_sketch:
--- @param parent table
--- @param width number|nil   nil when the host anchors both edges (LH, DW do)
--- @param opts table|nil     { hint = string|nil, icon = resolved path|nil, onChange = function(text, box)|nil }
--- @return EditBox  box, with box.hint (FontString) and box.icon (Texture|nil)
function lib.SearchBox(parent, width, opts)
-- Height 20 (the dropdown's). BackdropTemplate, SKIN fill and line. GameFontHighlightSmall. AutoFocus off.
-- Text insets (icon and 21 or 6, 6, 0, 0). Icon drawn at LEFT+5, 11x11, vertex 0.7,0.7,0.72.
-- Hint: GameFontDisableSmall at the text inset, shown iff text == ''.
-- Scripts SET by the constructor: OnTextChanged (hint, then opts.onChange(text or '', box)),
-- OnEscapePressed/OnEnterPressed -> ClearFocus, OnEditFocusGained/Lost -> line SKIN.focus / SKIN.line.
-- Contract: the host extends these with HookScript and never SetScripts them. W.Autocomplete(box, ...) composes after construction.
-- No setters: the host rewrites box.hint:SetText directly (DropWatcher's FB.Anchor does).

verdicts.name: W.SearchBox(parent, width, opts): flat filter-bar search box in the dropdown's skin
refutations: The three consumers check out. LootHistory modules/BrowserFilterBar.lua:404-424, BankLedger modules/Browser.lua:829-852 and DropWatcher modules/WindowFilterBar.lua:686-713 all set the same skin numbers, height 20 (DW K.CONTROL_H = 20 at core/Constants.lua:65), the same fonts and insets, a GameFontDisableSmall hint, and Esc/Enter -> ClearFocus. A repo-wide census of CreateFrame("EditBox") outside libs/tests finds only these three plus the analyst's correct exclusions (DW DetailCard.lua:647, MultiMeters Export_Modal.lua:789, PGFE Panel.lua:232,561). Bar 1 is cleared with the same semantics: all three are live filters, and the debounced and immediate apply differ only on the host side.

The gold focus line is not 'the dropdown's skin', and putting it into the library contradicts the candidate's own justification. W.Dropdown sets its border once (Widgets.lua:299) and never relights it. The only gold in Widgets.lua is the menu-row highlight (:100) and the row text (:151). Only DropWatcher (WindowFilterBar.lua:703-704) lights the line. Making it unconditional is the library imposing one consumer's choice on two others as a visible change, the decision bar 2 warns the library 'cannot make'. DW can keep it with two HookScript lines.

opts.icon has a single consumer (BankLedger MakeSearchMark, Browser.lua:755-766). Bar 2 allows one optional presentation argument, so it is permissible. But it is single-consumer surface frozen forever under the additive-only rule (library-stack.md:116), and BL can draw the mark itself after construction (CreateTexture plus box:SetTextInsets(21,6,0,0) plus box.hint:SetPoint) in about four lines.

The `width` parameter has no real consumer. LH and BL never set a width (both anchor two edges, BL via TOPLEFT and RIGHT). DW's SetSize(180, ...) at :688 is overwritten by FB.Anchor's two-edge anchoring (:746-750) and by CompactChrome.lua:392-398. Keeping it for symmetry with Dropdown(parent,width,opts) is fine, but it must be nil-able and documented as optional. It is not evidence of a need.

The anti-frequency rule cuts against this more than the analyst admits. Each copy is about 15 lines of backdrop and font calls with low semantic content. What carries the promotion is the 'two skins to keep in step' precedent in the Widgets.lua header (lines 6-10), not bar 1. The record should say that plainly.
missed_items: The proposed standard change edits library-stack.md:92 but misses that row's closing clause, '...and `Widgets.lua` stays at minor 12'. That clause becomes false at minor 13 and must be rewritten in the same edit.
DropWatcher rewrites box.hint in a second place, CompactChrome.lua:399 (L['Filter…'] in compact layout), not only FB.Anchor:751. Both are reasons box.hint must stay a public field of the contract.

LootHistory's B:SetSearchText (BrowserFilterBar.lua:130-138) calls self._onSearchText directly when SetText fires no OnTextChanged (headless kit or degraded install). The adoption must keep that host function as a named local that is passed as onChange and still stored on self, not turned into an anonymous closure.
DropWatcher's box also carries NS.Window.AttachTooltip(eb, ...) (:711), so the hook-based contract must cover the tooltip's OnEnter/OnLeave as well, not only the focus scripts.
The DW test tests/test_window_shell.lua:409-421 fires OnEditFocusGained/Lost and asserts the gold line. If gold is cut from the library, that assertion stays a host test on DW's hook.

Adoption cost: LH and BL are on v1.71.0 and DW on v1.72.0, so each adoption rides a multi-tag re-vendor (v1.72 through v1.75+) that brings unrelated contract changes. Sequence it with the revendor command's normal pass rather than as a standalone item.
scope_cuts: Drop the gold focus line and SKIN.focus from the library: the box wears exactly the dropdown's static skin. DropWatcher keeps its gold through eb:HookScript('OnEditFocusGained'/'OnEditFocusLost'). This also removes the analyst's only owner question and the visible change in LootHistory and BankLedger.

Drop opts.icon. BankLedger keeps MakeSearchMark host-side and adjusts the inset and hint point itself. If the owner wants the mark library-drawn, accept it as the single presentation argument, but then nothing else may join opts except hint and onChange.
Do not export SKIN or any constants (the analyst already keeps it file-local, which is correct).
Leave WidgetsAutocomplete's BORDER/BG untouched apart from a comment. Do not bump that file's minor for this.

A census of CreateFrame('CheckButton') and UICheckButtonTemplate in non-lib, non-test code across all repos finds only PremadeGroupsFilterExtension (EUISkin.lua and Panel.lua, deliberately native to match PGF), Outfitter (not on the roster) and a comment at LootHistory settings/Panel.lua:850 in the options panel. A flat bar button (LH and BL makeBarButton) is a separate nomination that should get its own issue if anyone wants it. analysis.cluster: LibKa0s#53: generalise Perf-1.0's PerfPanel into a shared StepPanel (Drop Watcher sim panel as the second consumer)

candidates.name: StepPanel: a host-driven clickable step panel (W.StepPanel in Widgets-1.0), with PerfPanel rebuilt on it
candidates.rationale: Only two things in the whole collection draw this panel. One is Perf's own panel inside the library (LibKa0s/LibKa0s/PerfPanel.lua, used by every Perf host and unchanged at panel minor 6 in all 14 vendored copies). The other is Drop Watcher's sim panel (DropWatcher/modules/SimPanel.lua). I searched the 14 roster addons (excluding libs/ and tests/_kit/) for step panels, checklists, wizards, dot-plus-label-plus-command rows, PanelStateOf, decorate and SimPanel. Every other hit is a /x perf slash string or a PerfSetup comment about Perf's own panel. Nobody else has a step panel. So promoting it gives one addon a public surface that stays forever (-1.0 is additive-only), to delete about 110 lines of frame code: SimPanel.lua:37-55 (constants), 400-458 (setColor, hover, newRow, paintRow) and parts of 576-615 (buildTitle, build, paintRows). The other ~570 lines stay in Drop Watcher anyway: Compose, Controls, the picker, the controls bar, docking, the saved point and the tooltip content. Rebuilding PerfPanel on it changes nothing a user sees. It touches a stable file (last change 88a59fb, 2026-09-30) that a 634-line suite guards, and it adds a new Perf→Widgets floor. Both consumers show the same look, but they disagree on what a row is and what a click does. Perf drives actionability from state and has unique keys. Drop Watcher computes actionability per row, so locked rows ahead of the current step are clickable and run RunTo. Its keys repeat ('step' on every timeline row), so it clicks by index. A render-only contract can absorb that, but only barely. The case changes if #54 (Sim-1.0) is accepted. The sim panel then moves into the library, StepPanel gets two in-library callers (Perf and Sim), and through Sim it reaches the six adopters #54 names. At that point it is part of the Sim work and no longer a standalone promotion. So: defer, tied to #54's decision. The answer to 'does it only make sense if #54 is promoted?' is yes.
candidates.bars: Bar 1, quoted: "Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape." It passes for presentation only, and narrowly. Same look: geometry ROW_W,ROW_H,GAP=360,22,4 / DOT_X,DOT=8,8 / LABEL_X=26 / CMD_PAD=10 / TITLE_H=24 / PAD=8 at PerfPanel.lua:32-37 and SimPanel.lua:38-41; palette at PerfPanel.lua:42-53 and SimPanel.lua:47-53; CMD_COLOR at :56 and :54; skin, close mark and UISpecialFrames at PerfPanel.lua:210-228 and SimPanel.lua:580,602-604. Different behaviour: Perf's actionable rule is state-based (PerfPanel.lua:100-103: ready|cancel|used) and Perf clicks a key through runCommand(step.command) (:141-145). Drop Watcher's actionable is per row and host-computed (SimPanel.lua:206-207, ahead rows), its keys are not unique (:205 key='step') and it clicks by index (:436, ClickRow :318-324). Hover reduces to one rule: on an actionable row, gold, except cancel, which is light red (PerfPanel.lua:135-139, SimPanel.lua:55,402-405). A render-only widget fed {label, command, state, actionable, tip} fits both, but bar 1 is met by one in-library caller plus one addon. Bar 2, quoted: "If adopting it requires a behavior flag per consumer, those flags are the consumers' divergence re-encoded as configuration ... One optional presentation argument is fine." It is borderline. Drop Watcher needs a check texture over the dot on a done row (SimPanel.lua:424-427,449-453), which Perf must not show if its look is to stay unchanged. It needs a footer slot that swaps between two bars and adds BAR_H to the height (:486-563,587,614). It needs per-row tooltips through its own NS.Window.AttachTooltip and NS.TipMarks (:437,182-193); the library has no tooltip helper, so this would have to be an onEnter hook. It needs host-owned positioning (dock and saved point, :353-398). Perf needs width-only resize (PerfPanel.lua:161-166), which Drop Watcher lacks, and the decorate hand-off (:204-208), which no host passes (CONSUMERS.md:275, zero). That is four or five options, mostly presentation. None changes what a click does, but the count is the warning sign. Bar 3, quoted: "A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code. Ask what would have to change for the shared version to be wrong, and whether that change is plausible this year." The Perf side is stable: 9 commits, the last on 2026-09-30. The Drop Watcher side is not: SimPanel.lua has 7 commits between 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-18 (ac5c5a6, d16329d, 1753c1d, e955661, 0c42908, 7d2c627, 2bfef72), most recently the G6 tooltip reformat. The shared core (row geometry and palette) has not moved; the parts that keep changing are host-owned. It passes only if the contract stays render-only. Anti-pattern check: 'MUST NOT promote on frequency alone' does not apply, because the frequency is two. On cost, the precedent is DebugLog's hard Widgets floor (DebugLog.lua:26-33) for CopyWindow, which was taken after a fifth copy, not a second.
verified_consumers: LibKa0s LibKa0s/PerfPanel.lua:60-70 (STEPS is a file-local constant), :93-96 (PanelStateOf reads P.Progress()), :74 (__AttachPanel): a real consumer, the reference look. Semantics: fixed 6 rows, state-driven actionability, key-unique, command runs through the host slash, no tooltips, width-resizable, optional decorate

LibKa0s Perf hosts: nine addons ship core/PerfSetup.lua (AbsorbTracker, AuraMaster, ConsumableMaster, DropWatcher, KickCD, LootHistory, MultiMeters, PartyFrameEnhanced, QuickComms). All 14 vendored PerfPanel.lua copies are at PANEL_MINOR 6 (line 13). These hosts are consumers of Perf, not of a step panel: none passes `decorate` (AbsorbTracker/core/PerfSetup.lua:113 records its removal), so none would see a change

DropWatcher modules/SimPanel.lua:37-55,400-458,576-615: a real copy (the geometry, palette, rows and frame match PerfPanel). Same look, different row and click semantics: per-row actionable including 'ahead' locked rows (:206-207), non-unique key 'step' (:205), click by index into RunTo (:303-324,436), check texture on done (:424-427,449-453), tooltips (:437), footer picker and controls (:486-563), height follows rows plus bar (:614), dock and saved point (:353-398), stand-down hide (:683-685). No 'used' state (:47-53)
DropWatcher docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:301: the documented-deviation row for the copy. Its re-check trigger is 'LibKa0s#53 lands'; last re-checked 2026-10-14 against v1.72.0 (DW-P22)

No other consumer exists. Grep over AbsorbTracker, AuraMaster, BankLedger, ConsumableMaster, KickCD, LootHistory, MultiMeters, PanelMaster, PartyFrameEnhanced, PremadeGroupsFilterExtension, PrettyChat, QuickComms (on master in the working tree) and WhatGroup found only /x perf help strings (for example QuickComms/settings/Slash.lua:58, ConsumableMaster/settings/Slash.lua:179, LootHistory/settings/Schema.lua:1114) and PerfSetup comments. The 'checklist' hits (LootHistory/core/Constants.lua:232, WhatGroup/settings/Schema.lua:163) are settings MultiCheck rows, not step panels. LootHistory/modules/Timeline.lua is a line chart. DropWatcher/modules/OfferPanel.lua is a candidate table

challenge.cluster: LibKa0s#53: generalise Perf-1.0's PerfPanel into a shared StepPanel (Drop Watcher sim panel as the second consumer)

verdicts.name: StepPanel: a host-driven clickable step panel (W.StepPanel in Widgets-1.0), with PerfPanel rebuilt on it
refutations: I agree with defer, and the evidence supports it more strongly than the analyst says. Bar 1 in library-stack.md:228 ('Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape') fails on semantics, not just narrowly. In PerfPanel.lua:136-145 the library decides actionability itself (state ready|cancel|used) and a click runs exactly one slash verb. In SimPanel.lua:204-207 the host computes actionability per row, so locked 'ahead' rows are clickable, and SimPanel.lua:318-324 ClickRow re-composes the rows and runs several steps through RunTo (:303-312) or start/stop. The two copies share pixels (SimPanel.lua:37-55 against PerfPanel.lua:32-56). The worked example at library-stack.md:228-230 ('two addons filtering records is not two consumers of one filter') is this case

Even in the analyst's own conditional plan, 'IF #54 is accepted, StepPanel gets two in-library callers' does not justify a PUBLIC W.StepPanel. Perf and Sim would both live inside the library, so the reuse can be a library-private file whose fields are not listed in lib.MODULES or docs/api. That avoids the additive-only permanent contract (library-stack.md:222-224). The analyst jumps from 'shared inside the library' to 'public Widgets export' without arguing for it

The '#54 names six adopters' that StepPanel would reach through Sim are adopters of the SIMULATOR, not of a step panel. The #54 text (tool-results/bgbu69fq0.txt, the #54 Adopters section) lists LootHistory, BankLedger, MultiMeters, WhatGroup, KickCD and DropWatcher as having filed issues, and none of them has any Sim code yet. They are speculative future consumers and must not count toward bar 1 for the panel

Bar 2 (library-stack.md:231-233) is failed, not borderline. The descriptor the analyst sketches has check, footer{height,build,paint}, resizable, decorate, a per-row actionable override and tip. decorate exists only for Perf and has zero live hosts. resizable='width' exists only for Perf, and the check exists only for DW. Each one is a single consumer's divergence turned into configuration

My grep found no missed consumers. Across all 14 roster addons (excluding libs/ and tests/_kit), DOT_X/LABEL_X/CMD_PAD/StepPanel and similar patterns hit only SimPanel.lua. The other hits are unrelated: PremadeGroupsFilterExtension/modules/Panel.lua:48 is a checkbox LABEL_X, LootHistory/modules/AnalyticsCharts.lua:15 is LABEL_X_ADJUST on a chart, and BankLedger/MultiMeters/QuickComms are color-texture coincidences. QuickComms is on master in the working tree. The analyst's census holds

Minor accuracy point: the hover rules differ in what triggers them as well as in the colours. Perf decides from state (PerfPanel.lua:136-139: ready/used gold, cancel light red). DW decides from row.actionable plus a HOVER table (SimPanel.lua:55,402-405), and that table has no 'used' entry and does have a 'locked' one.
