analysis.cluster: LibKa0s#54: LibKa0s-Sim-1.0, a shared in-game simulator lifted from Drop Watcher's /dw sim

candidates.name: LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 as proposed: a new major with Session, Seam, Fire, Timeline and the panel
candidates.rationale: Exactly one consumer exists, Drop Watcher, and no other roster addon has any simulator code: a grep for simulat|Sim.|SetProvider over core/, modules/ and settings/ of all 13 other addons finds 0 files. The five 'adopter' issues are templated wish-list entries filed in one batch by DW-91 on 2026-10-11 between 10:15:57Z and 10:17:40Z. Each is triaged severity:low, with no spec, branch or code behind it. None of the five meets the host contract the issue sets as a prerequisite (one dispatch table, every simulated client read routed through NS.Compat). Most of the code the issue calls generic is in fact Drop Watcher's: Sim.lua's stop steps name nine DW modules, Fire is bound to DW's fan-out FEATURE_EVENTS dispatcher, and the scenario timeline's PLAY table is DW's loot or encounter drivers. Taking that into a new major now would add additive-only surface the library keeps forever, shaped around one addon. That is the failure library-stack-§7 says is 'harder to reverse'.
candidates.bars:
library-stack-§7, 'What earns promotion into a Ka0s-owned lib (MUST)': 'A shape MUST clear all three bars before it moves upstream'.

Bar 1, quoted: 'Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape.' FAILS. There is one consumer (DropWatcher). LootHistory#37, BankLedger#24, MultiMeters#60, WhatGroup#24 and KickCD#38 exist, all OPEN, enhancement, state:triaged, severity:low, created 2026-10-11 10:15-10:17Z, with identical templated bodies and no comments. Each says 'Build on LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 ... once it ships', so each depends on this issue rather than providing independent demand. Their event plumbing shows the semantics would not match either (see verified_consumers).

Bar 2, quoted: 'No per-consumer escape hatches. If adopting it requires a behavior flag per consumer, those flags are the consumers' divergence re-encoded as configuration ... a flag that changes what the function does is the tell.' FAILS as proposed. The issue's own safety rule says 'it refuses to start in a real group, an instance or combat (each host can relax this)', and every adopter issue repeats 'unless this addon has a reason to allow it'. That is a behavior flag per consumer. The refusal inputs themselves are host-specific: DW reads NS.Situations.ReadInputs and NS.Restrictions.InCombat (DropWatcher/modules/Sim.lua:117-123), and Refusal also checks DW's State.testMode and NS.StoodDownRefusal (Sim.lua:127-137). The stop order is DW policy too (Sim.lua:340-350, plus the CancelQueued-before-seam-off rule at :367-371). A shared Session would need hooks for each of these, which is the same tell in another form.

Bar 3, quoted: 'A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code. Ask what would have to change for the shared version to be wrong, and whether that change is plausible this year.' FAILS. The seam depends on three things a host could easily change. (a) The whole compat family loads before the seam and nothing caches a member at load; this is enforced only by DW's TOC comments, DropWatcher.toc:54-67 ('Read inside functions only'). (b) Plain world reads are routed through NS.Compat; DW created core/CompatWorld.lua for this (DropWatcher.toc:56-58), but compat-§1 requires routing only 'deprecated or version-variant' calls, and its applicability condition says 'a file of pass-through aliases is not required and not wanted'. (c) Event dispatch has DW's fan-out shape. The compat-family rule itself only changed at v2.79.0 (2026-10-11), the same day the sim landed.

Also quoted: 'MUST NOT promote on frequency alone' does not apply, since frequency is 1. 'SHOULD record a rejection with its reason where the next author will look' applies to this deferral.
verified_consumers: DropWatcher/core/SimSeam.lua:129-133: wraps every non-PURE function in NS.Compat at load. The only real consumer; 142 lines.

DropWatcher/modules/Sim.lua:145-157: deliver() walks NS.FEATURE_EVENTS rows {event, methodName} and calls NS.addon[method] under pcall. Fan-out to several handlers per event is DW's own dispatcher (DropWatcher/core/DropWatcher.lua:44-47 builds per-event lists).
DropWatcher/modules/Sim.lua:340-350: ENGINE_STEPS names NS.LootFeed, NS.Inspect, NS.Roster, NS.History, NS.TradeTimer, NS.Situations and NS.Window, and :369 names NS.Asks. All DW-specific.
DropWatcher/modules/Sim.lua:229-269: SetRestriction and SetLockdown, plus providers for IsRestrictionActive and InChatMessagingLockdown. DW's restriction model.

LootHistory#37: FALSE CONSUMER today. It has no single dispatch table: capture events are a local list registered on private bus targets (LootHistory/modules/Reconciler.lua:689-694; 'two private bus targets ... __ev carries the capture events'). About 23 direct client reads sit outside core/Compat.lua by a rough grep. No sim code.

BankLedger#24: FALSE CONSUMER today. It splits OPEN_EVENTS, CLOSE_EVENTS, CHANGE_EVENTS and GUILD_DATA_EVENTS (BankLedger/modules/Ledger.lua:806-822), and guild-bank open and close come from GuildBankFrame OnShow/OnHide hooks (comment at Ledger.lua:802-804), which Fire(event) cannot drive. No sim code.

MultiMeters#60: closest in shape but FALSE CONSUMER today. A local EVENTS {event, method} table (MultiMeters/core/MultiMeters.lua:125-140) is not a FEATURE_EVENTS fan-out. Its C_DamageMeter shims are per-member functions in core/Compat.lua:84-110, so providers could answer them, but about 17 direct client reads sit outside Compat. No sim code.

WhatGroup#24: FALSE CONSUMER. Its key input is hooksecurefunc(C_LFGList, 'ApplyToGroup', ...) (WhatGroup/core/WhatGroup.lua:85) and a SetItemRef hook (:149). These are hooks, not events, and Fire cannot deliver them. Events are registered directly (:376-383). About 22 direct client reads sit outside Compat.

KickCD#38: FALSE CONSUMER. Unit events are registered per unit on per-filter frames with RegisterUnitEvent (KickCD/core/Util.lua:525-533). Dispatch maps are per module {EVENT = method} (KickCD/modules/Castbar.lua:120, IconGrid.lua:90). Unit existence and hostility are read directly from _G (KickCD/core/State.lua:90-91, 118). A Compat seam cannot answer any of that.

QuickComms (master 12da802) and PremadeGroupsFilterExtension: the only other NS.FEATURE_EVENTS hosts (QuickComms/core/QuickComms.lua:21, PGFE/core/PGFE.lua:33). Both register each row with AceEvent RegisterEvent(row[1], row[2]) (QuickComms.lua:28-29, PGFE.lua:41-42): one handler per event, not DW's fan-out, so the semantics differ. Neither has a sim issue or sim code. The issue does not mention QuickComms at all, either as an adopter or as ruled out.
false_or_stale_claims: 'Drop Watcher's implementation (about 3,400 lines ...)': 3412 is the whole DW sim (9 files). The four files called generic total 1570 (SimSeam 142, Sim 403, SimScenario 340, SimPanel 685). The truly host-neutral logic inside them is about 300-350 lines: the wrap/provider/Live seam, the cleanup list, After/timers, the delivering flag and the step cursor.

'modules/SimScenario.lua: a timeline of steps with Run, Step, RunTo ...': RunTo is in modules/SimPanel.lua:303, not SimScenario. SimScenario also carries the DW-only SCENARIOS (:71-78), the PLAY drivers bound to NS.SimEvents and NS.SimReport (:125-146), and the start that builds NS.SimPool and NS.SimRoster and opens NS.Window (:288-327).
'These files are generic' (Sim.lua): the session's stop steps, refusal inputs, restriction model and Fire's dispatcher are all DW-specific (Sim.lua:117-137, 145-157, 229-269, 340-371).

'Safety rules ... enforced by the library': four of the five cannot be. 'Nothing is sent' and 'never acts on a real player' hold only for members the host lists as guarded (SimSeam.lua:75-79); a send outside NS.Compat is invisible. 'Saved data is never written' is DW's History.lua writing a session log (Sim.lua:30-31, 346); no library can intercept SavedVariables writes. 'Stop cleans everything' depends on the host registering every cleanup. Only the refusal can be library-side, and the issue then makes it relaxable per host.

'every client read the simulator must answer goes through the Compat family (compat-§1, standard v2.79.0)': compat-§1 and v2.79.0 cover only 'deprecated or version-variant' client calls and the family split. They do not require routing plain reads, and the applicability condition says a pass-through-alias file is 'not required and not wanted'. The prerequisite is a new rule, not an existing one.

'Issues have been filed in each' (adopters): the issues exist (LootHistory#37, BankLedger#24, MultiMeters#60, WhatGroup#24, KickCD#38), but they are a single templated batch that depends on this issue, not independent demand. None of the five meets the host contract today (see verified_consumers).
The adopter and ruled-out lists omit QuickComms, a roster addon with test mode and a FEATURE_EVENTS table.
candidates.api_sketch: Not proposed now. If the recheck trigger fires, the earliest a major could look like this is: Sim = LibStub('LibKa0s-Sim-1.0'); local seam = Sim.NewSeam(NS.Compat, { pure = {...}, guarded = { Key = fn } }) giving seam:SetProvider(key, fn), seam:Live(fn, ...), seam:Keys() and seam.active; local session = Sim.NewSession({ seam = seam, refusal = function() ... end, deliver = function(event, ...) ... end }) giving session:Start(opts), session:Stop(reason), session:AddCleanup(fn), session:After(delay, fn), session:Fire(event, ...) and session:IsDelivering(). The refusal and deliver callbacks are the host seams. Timeline, scenarios, providers, stop order and the panel stay host code until a second host shows the same semantics.
libka0s_changes: None now. Leave issue #54 open with state:triaged and post a comment recording the deferral, the bar-by-bar reasons above and the recheck trigger. Or close it as will-not-do with the same record; that choice is for the owner.

If it is later accepted, the cost of a new major is: LibKa0s/Sim.lua (plus any secondary files) with lib.MODULES.Sim = 1; LibKa0s/LibKa0s.xml <Script> entries; a tests/majors.lua entry (the versioning suite and tools/gen-api-members.lua read it); docs/api/Sim/version-1-docs.md and a docs/api/CONSUMERS.md row; headless suites for seam wrap and guard, Live bypass, stop order under pcall, timer cancel and Fire isolation; a CHANGELOG version block naming Sim 1; a Core floor declaration; and test-kit mocks for C_Timer.NewTimer if missing (Kit.VERSION bumps only if the kit changes). Semver minor, e.g. v1.76.0.
standard_changes: Optional patch bump (v2.85.x). open-evolutions.md, 'Further LibKa0s modules' entry: add one sentence recording 'LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 (LibKa0s#54) deferred: one consumer (DropWatcher); recheck when a second addon ships a simulator.' This follows §7's 'SHOULD record a rejection with its reason where the next author will look'.

If accepted later: recount library-stack-§7's module table and open-evolutions' figure from tests/majors.lua and LibKa0s.xml rather than incrementing them. Also add a §7 table row for Sim and a minor bump.

LootHistory#37, BankLedger#24, MultiMeters#60, WhatGroup#24, KickCD#38: comment on each, spaced out, saying LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 is deferred. Any simulator built there starts in-addon from DropWatcher's reference. List the addon's specific blockers (from verified_consumers) as prerequisites. Keep or close per the owner's answer.
No code adoption in any addon.
candidates.recheck_trigger: Reopen the promotion question when a second roster addon has a merged in-addon simulator, built from DW's reference, and it routes simulated reads through NS.Compat and delivers events through a host dispatch table. At that point, diff the two seams and sessions line by line: only the parts with identical semantics (no per-host behavior flags) are candidates. Also re-check if compat-§1 is ever widened to require all client reads in the compat family.
risks: Accepting now would freeze DW's load-order and dispatch assumptions into additive-only library surface. The second real consumer would then need escape hatches, as happened with the rejected schema-migration runner.

The seam only sees host NS.Compat. Reads that LibKa0s majors make for a host (for example Env-1.0's map ID and zone, Item-1.0's cache) bypass it, so a simulated world leaks real answers unless each host wraps those too.
Deferring leaves five open adopter issues whose 'How' sections point at a library that will not ship. They should be repointed so nobody blocks on #54.

candidates.name: Minimal core: the Compat answer seam only (wrap, SetProvider, guarded members, Live)
candidates.rationale: This is the most host-neutral piece: SimSeam.lua is 142 lines, and its logic (lines 95-133) is about 40 lines once DW's PURE and GUARDED data is removed. It was evaluated as the accept-minimal option and still fails bar 1, because it has one consumer. Its correctness also rests on a host load-order contract the library cannot check. The wrap captures each member's value at wrap time, so a member added or replaced after the seam runs, or cached in a local before it, escapes simulation silently. Shipping it would also bless a stricter Compat-routing rule the standard does not hold. Forty lines a host can copy are cheaper than a major with a load-order contract.
candidates.bars:
Bar 1 ('Two or more consumers, with the same semantics'): FAILS, with DropWatcher/core/SimSeam.lua:129-133 the only instance. No other addon wraps NS.Compat. MultiMeters is the only named adopter whose data source is reachable through per-member Compat functions (MultiMeters/core/Compat.lua:84-110), and it has no simulator.

Bar 2 ('No per-consumer escape hatches'): would PASS. The pure and guarded lists are data describing the host's members, not behavior flags. Guarded answers are host functions too, since DW's printSend and handOver use NS.Print and NS.L (SimSeam.lua:55-79).

Bar 3 ('A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code'): WEAK. It relies on TOC order (DropWatcher.toc:54-67) and on no host caching members at load. A future compat split, or a LibKa0s-Compat-1.0 member added to NS.Compat after the seam runs, breaks it silently. The compat family rule changed as recently as v2.79.0.
verified_consumers: DropWatcher/core/SimSeam.lua:95-133: the only consumer.
No other roster addon: 0 files match SetProvider|simulat|Sim. outside DropWatcher.
false_or_stale_claims: 'Seam(compatTable, { pure = {...}, guarded = {...} })' as a library guarantee that 'nothing is sent': it guards only what the host lists. A send outside the compat family goes out.
candidates.api_sketch: Sim.NewSeam(compat, { pure = { Key = true }, guarded = { Key = fn } }) -> seam with seam.active, seam:SetProvider(key, fn|nil), seam:Answer(key, live, ...), seam:Live(fn, ...) and seam:Keys(). Deferred.

candidates.name: Timeline step machine (Step, Run, Pause, Resume, Restart, RunTo, listeners)
candidates.rationale: The cursor, tick, pause, resume and listener logic (SimScenario.lua:165-280) is generic in shape, but it has one consumer. It is welded to DW's PLAY drivers, NS.Sim.After timers and DW's printed step lines. RunTo is the panel's (SimPanel.lua:303). Whether any shared step list belongs in the library is LibKa0s#53's question; it should not enter through a Sim major.
candidates.bars: Bar 1 ('Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape'): FAILS. The only consumer is DropWatcher/modules/SimScenario.lua. Perf's step flow has the same shape but different semantics: no auto-play, no pause, no timer. Bar 2: the step-delay setting (SimScenario.lua:39-58 reads DW's 'sim.stepDelay' profile key) and the per-kind drivers would be host callbacks, which is acceptable, but nothing exists to test them against. Bar 3: the timeline is shaped by DW's encounter model (pull, lockdownOn, kill, loot, lockdownOff, at :89-100). It is not shown to be stable.
verified_consumers: DropWatcher/modules/SimScenario.lua:165-280: the only consumer.
LibKa0s/LibKa0s/PerfPanel.lua:60 (STEPS): a different semantics (user-run fixed steps). Not a consumer.
false_or_stale_claims: The issue lists RunTo under SimScenario. It is SimPanel.lua:303.

challenge.cluster: LibKa0s#54: LibKa0s-Sim-1.0, a shared in-game simulator lifted from Drop Watcher's /dw sim

verdicts.name: LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 as proposed: a new major with Session, Seam, Fire, Timeline and the panel
refutations: Re-verified bar 1 against all 14 roster addons (AbsorbTracker, AuraMaster, BankLedger, ConsumableMaster, DropWatcher, KickCD, LootHistory, MultiMeters, Outfitter, PanelMaster, PartyFrameEnhanced, PGFE, PrettyChat, QuickComms, WhatGroup checkouts): grep -Ei 'simulat|SetProvider|NS\.Sim\b' over core/, modules/ and settings/ hits only DropWatcher. One consumer, so bar 1 ('Two or more consumers, with the same semantics', library-stack.md:228) fails. The analyst is correct.

Confirmed that the DW-specific coupling is in the 'generic' files: Sim.Refusal reads NS.StoodDownRefusal, State.testMode, NS.Situations.ReadInputs and NS.Restrictions.InCombat (DropWatcher/modules/Sim.lua:117-137). ENGINE_STEPS names NS.LootFeed/Roster/History/TradeTimer/Situations/Window (Sim.lua:340-350). NS.Asks.CancelQueued must run before the seam goes off (Sim.lua:367-371). deliver() walks NS.FEATURE_EVENTS with a pcall per row (Sim.lua:145-157).

Confirmed the dispatch semantics differ. DW fans out several handlers per event (handlersByEvent, DropWatcher/core/DropWatcher.lua:42-50, and ARCHITECTURE.md:165, where PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD has 7 handlers through OnSharedFeatureEvent). QuickComms (now on master) and PGFE register one handler per row through NS.SafeRegisterEvent (QuickComms/core/QuickComms.lua:28-29, PGFE/core/PGFE.lua:41-42), and AceEvent holds one handler per event per target. Small citation fix: both use NS.SafeRegisterEvent (QuickComms/core/CoreSetup.lua:63), not a bare AceEvent RegisterEvent as the analyst wrote. The conclusion stands.
The issue's 'each host can relax this' (issue text, refusal bullet) is a behavior flag per consumer. That is the tell in bar 2 (library-stack.md:231-234), so the analyst's bar-2 failure is right.
missed_items: Payload weight is an argument against acceptance that the analyst did not cite. library-stack.md:108 makes the ship payload 'the whole folder, always', and only media/icons is carved out. A Sim major (about 300-1570 lines) would be vendored into and loaded by all 14 addons, and 13 of them would never call it. One consumer would put load cost on every other addon.

Analyst's addon_adoptions item 'add a docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Documented deviations row for the sim seam' is wrong. DropWatcher/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:289-292 reserves that table for ratified deviations from the standard. No LibKa0s major provides a simulator, so in-addon sim code violates nothing: anti-pattern #47 forbids hand-rolling only what a module already provides. The SimPanel row (:301) exists because PerfPanel exists. The seam and session have no such counterpart. Record the re-check trigger on #54 and, optionally, in open-evolutions, not as a deviation.

If this is ever revisited, consider whether the headless pieces belong in testkit/ rather than the runtime payload: event firing and timer stepping. The test kit is not a consumer, but it bears on where a future shared piece would live and what it would weigh.
scope_cuts: Do not ship any part of the major: Session, Seam, Fire, Timeline, the scenarios or the panel.

candidates.name: C2 (#57): fix the stale 'install missing the art' comments in Core, DebugLog and OptionsIdList (comment-only, fold into v1.75.0)
candidates.rationale: Pruning makes these comments wrong. `Media.Icon` answers a path for any catalog name and never looks at the disk (Media.lua:264-273; library-stack-§7: 'does not look at the disk and MUST NOT be taught to'). So an undeclared icon gives a BLANK control. It does not fall back to the × or to the text button. Core.lua:224-228 claims the × is 'what every window gets on an install missing the art', and DebugLog.lua:229-235 says makeIconButton is 'nil when there is no art to draw' and that the text button is what 'an install missing the art gets'. Both describe a fallback that cannot happen. The issue missed a third site: OptionsIdList.lua:227-229 says '`media/icons/info.tga` ships inside the vendored payload', which is now true only when a host declares `info`. The same block also has stale line cites: `KCM.Icon("info")` is at ConsumableMaster settings/Category.lua:654, not :641; DebugLog's lookup is at DebugLog.lua:241-244, not :179-182; ICONS is at Media.lua:94-99, not :92-96. All three files go to every consumer in the coming mass re-vendor anyway. Folding the fixes into v1.75.0 costs three comment-only minor bumps now and saves a forgotten fix later. The same comments would mislead whoever reads them while debugging the first blank icon after pruning, which is the moment they matter most. The library's own precedent is that comment-only changes still bump (CHANGELOG.md:4639, :6770).

candidates.rationale: I derived every roster addon's exact icon list from real draw sites. Grepping `Media.Icon(` / `M.Icon(` alone, as #57 suggests, finds none of them. Addons resolve through their NS.Icon or KCM.Icon seam (core/MediaSetup.lua in each), through NS.IconMarkup (LootHistory), through data tables (`art =`, `icon =`), through constants (HANDLE_ICON) and through library calls. The library-drawn names are verified in the payload: `close` from Core.MakeCloseButton with an addonName (Core.lua:241-242; reached from DebugLog.lua:278, PerfPanel.lua:210 and Widgets.lua:552, and DebugLog's own copy window passes `d.addonName or d.name`, DebugLog.lua:724); `copy` and `clear` from DebugLog.lua:292-293; `info` from OptionsIdList.lua:508, drawn only when an entry carries help (:854, `hasHelp`). All 14 addons pass `addonName` to DebugLog, so all 14 declare at least `clear, close, copy`. `info` is declared only where something actually draws it: AuraMaster's id lists carry help (Filters.lua:860, GeneralSpells.lua:920), while BankLedger's (Panel.lua:239, entries `{id=id}`) and LootHistory's (no help) do not. Per the owner's 2026-10-20 bare-minimum ruling, addons that never draw `info` do not declare it. With these lines every addon except QuickComms goes from about 28 MB of icons (v1.74.0) to 8-52 KB. The issue misses a blocker: 9 addons have a test that opens `libs/LibKa0s/media/icons/<name>.tga` for EVERY `Media.ICONS` entry. That test fails at the v1.75.0 copy even before pruning, because the catalog now holds `ph:`/`gi:` names that have no flat file. Separately, 8 addons have an `info.tga must exist` test that fails once `info` is pruned. Both have to be rewritten in the re-vendor commit.

candidates.name: C6 (#57): close the set of library-drawn icon names (close, copy, clear, info) against cross-copy minor skew
candidates.rationale: New finding, not in either issue. library-stack-§7 says 'A pruned copy cannot break another addon' because `Icon` builds the path from the caller's folder. That holds for names the HOST passes. It does not hold for names the LIBRARY resolves on the host's behalf when copies are skewed. LibStub serves the highest minor of each file from whichever addon carries it. Suppose a future DebugLog (vendored only by addon A) starts drawing a fifth catalog name in the console title bar. Addon B, still on v1.75.0 and pruned to `clear, close, copy`, then gets B's console built by A's newer DebugLog, which calls `Media.Icon("B", <new>)` (the DebugLog.lua:241-244 pattern) into B's pruned folder. The button is blank, and B's own gate stays green because B's vendored copy never draws that name. The standard's current remedy ('a library release that draws a new icon on a host's behalf MUST say so in its changelog, as a re-vendor note') only helps hosts that have re-vendored. The library already has the skew-safe pattern for new chrome: Widgets/DragHandle/Dropdown take RESOLVED art from the host (`helpIcon`, `closeIcon`, `chevron`, `check`, `handleIcon`; Widgets.lua:12-16, WidgetsDragHandle.lua:43-44). Freezing the library-drawn set at today's four names and requiring new library chrome to take host-resolved paths keeps pruning safe for good. #56 (icon styling / glows) is the next likely place a library module would want to draw catalog art.
candidates.bars: Promotion bars: not applicable. Standard text it corrects, quoted from library-stack-§7: 'A pruned copy cannot break another addon. LibStub serves one copy of each Media file to every host, but `Icon` builds the path from the caller's folder name' and 'a library release that draws a new icon on a host's behalf MUST say so in its changelog, as a re-vendor note.'
verified_consumers: Library-drawn today, from the host's folder: Core.lua:241-242 (close), DebugLog.lua:241-244 with :292-293 (copy, clear), OptionsIdList.lua:503-511 (info). All other library chrome takes resolved paths (Widgets.lua:12-16, :548-553; WidgetsDragHandle.lua:405, :607).
Every roster addon pairs its own minors with whatever LibStub picks; consumers sit at v1.71.0, v1.72.0 and v1.74.0 today (CLAUDE.md provenance lines), so skew is the normal state.

verdicts.name: C6 (#57): close the set of library-drawn icon names against cross-copy minor skew
refutations: The hazard is real and the current standard text is wrong. library-stack.md:198-202 says 'A pruned copy cannot break another addon ... each host's paths point into its own libs/LibKa0s/media/icons/ and draw from what that host declared.' Under LibStub, the newest DebugLog/Core/OptionsIdList copy (from any host) resolves names on behalf of every host (Core.lua:241-242, DebugLog.lua:241-244, OptionsIdList.lua:503-511). So a name added in a later minor draws blank in a pruned host that has not re-vendored, and that host's gate stays green. The existing remedy (library-stack.md:186-187, a changelog re-vendor note) only reaches hosts that re-vendor.
The analyst calls this cluster-external, but it directly qualifies the #57 rule, so it is in scope.

A bare 'closed forever' rule may later be broken by an additive need (for example #56). An exception procedure is better than a rule that gets quietly ignored.

analysis.cluster: LibKa0s #56: promote IconStyle and LibCustomGlow glow driving into a new major (working name LibKa0s-IconStyle-1.0)

candidates.name: IconStyle half: Config / ApplyIcon / PaintBorder / PaintRing as a LibKa0s major
candidates.rationale: Every icon-styling consumer means something different by 'style an icon'. The only code that is identical everywhere is a one-line symmetric SetTexCoord crop and a 4-line LSM 'Solid' registration, which is too little to justify a major. DW's border is quality-colored, generation-cached and drawn over the art on the button itself. QC's carries size, desaturate, alpha, a tint multiplied by the glyph color, and a round ring built from QC's own disc texture and wedge width. KickCD's border is a prebuilt frame with an unclamped 0.08 zoom. AuraMaster insets the art inside the border, corrects zoom for aspect ratio and guards the border against secrets. ConsumableMaster keeps zoom in percent (0..40)/100. A shared Config would need per-consumer flags for each of these, which bar 2 calls 'the consumers' divergence re-encoded as configuration'.
candidates.bars: Bar 1 ('Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape'): FAILS. DW IconStyle.Apply (DropWatcher/modules/IconStyle.lua:137-148) caches on gen+link and colors the border by item quality (110-131, QualityColor 100-108). QC IconStyle.Config/ApplyIcon (QuickComms/modules/IconStyle.lua:87-119) adds size/desaturate/alpha/tint and has no per-button cache. QC PaintRing (156-175) depends on NS.DialSlices.DISC and NS.DialLayout.WEDGE, both host-only. AuraMaster layoutIcon (AuraMaster/modules/Style_Icons.lua:80-96) corrects zoom by aspect ratio and insets the art, and Style.lua:186-201 shrinks the icon by 2*inset. These shapes look alike but behave differently. Bar 2 ('No per-consumer escape hatches... a flag that changes what the function does is the tell'): FAILS. Quality coloring, the ring vs square choice, inset vs overlay, aspect correction and the zoom unit would each be a behavior flag. Bar 3 ('A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code'): FAILS. QC's look grew in two days (Icons tab B9 on 2026-10-19, then the Buttons-tab glow on 2026-10-20), so the abstraction is still moving. 'MUST NOT promote on frequency alone': the remaining shared bit (z,1-z,z,1-z) is the high-frequency, low-content shape the rule names.
verified_consumers: DropWatcher modules/IconStyle.lua:54-57 (LSM 'Solid'), 71-76 (borderTexture + tooltip fallback), 145 (zoom), 110-131 (border on button child, item-quality color): only the zoom and Solid lines match QC

QuickComms modules/IconStyle.lua:41-44, 52-56 (same Solid/fallback), 113-119 ApplyIcon (desat/alpha/tint x glyph color, QC-only), 123-131 IconFrame anchored to btn.qcIcon (not the button), 156-175 PaintRing (host textures): partial match only

KickCD modules/IconGrid_Render.lua:792-813 ApplyAppearance: zoom default 0.08 with no clamp, border on prebuilt self.border, its own fetchBorderTexture (line 54) with a different fallback name: different semantics
AuraMaster modules/Style.lua:186-201 and Style_Icons.lua:80-96: inset art, aspect-corrected zoom, GuardedBorder: different semantics (false candidate)
ConsumableMaster modules/MacroBarButton.lua:339-344: zoom in percent 0..40: different unit
No other roster addon (AbsorbTracker, BankLedger, LootHistory, MultiMeters, PanelMaster, PartyFrameEnhanced, PGFE, PrettyChat, WhatGroup) styles icons with zoom plus border.

DW IconStyle+Glow are 156+185=341 lines and QC's are 175+236=411, both including headers and host-only policy (KindOf, QualityColor, Sent/timers, Button glow, Refresh). The portion actually common to both hosts is about 40-50 lines (Solid registration, borderTexture, START/STOP, spendBurst).

candidates.name: Stateless LibCustomGlow-1.0 driver: Start/Stop one of the four styles from a style name + knob values under a key
candidates.rationale: This is the one genuinely shared piece. DW and QC have byte-for-byte the same START/STOP tables (QC's adds a key parameter), and KickCD's startEffect/StopGlow has the same mapping from knob to LCG positional argument, with the same traps: pixelLength 0 must become nil, and pixelBorder must be a boolean because nil draws the dark border. So bar 1 passes for a stateless Start/Stop. Bar 2 passes with key as an identity argument and frameLevel as the one optional presentation argument. It is still about 35 lines per host, three sites, and all three work today with the same LCG minor (24). Promoting it means a 16th major with no floor on a third-party library the standard does not yet list (library-stack-§2 has no LibCustomGlow row), a doc set, a test file, a module-table recount, and characterization-first re-vendors in three addons. Under the owner's very high bar, that cost is not earned yet. Hold it until a fourth consumer arrives or the copies drift.
candidates.bars: Bar 1 ('Two or more consumers, with the same semantics'): PASSES for the stateless mapping, with three consumers. DW START/STOP (DropWatcher/modules/Glow.lua:249-277), QC START/STOP (QuickComms/modules/Glow.lua:230-258) and KickCD startEffect/StopGlow (KickCD/modules/IconGrid_Render.lua:448-470, 388-396) map the same knobs to the same LCG arguments. Two differences are presentational: KickCD passes no frameLevel (it raises its own glow child to level+5 at line 274), and KickCD stops all four styles unconditionally where DW and QC stop the recorded one. Bar 2 ('One optional presentation argument is fine; a flag that changes what the function does is the tell'): PASSES if limited to Start(frame, style, color, knobs, key, frameLevel?) and Stop(frame, style?, key). Bar 3 ('Ask what would have to change for the shared version to be wrong, and whether that change is plausible this year'): MARGINAL. It is bound to LCG's positional _Start signatures, which are stable at minor 24 in all three hosts. But the library cannot floor on LCG, because a consumer-vendored lib cannot be in the payload, and a host on an older LCG lacking ProcGlow_Start would hit the library's call, so each member needs its own presence guard. 'MUST NOT promote on frequency alone': three sites of moderate content (the nil/boolean traps are real content), so the rule does not reject it, but it does not compel promotion either. Soft-resolving LCG at call time is ALLOWED by §7 precedent: 'LibKa0s-Bus-1.0 resolves AceEvent-3.0 at call time and answers nil from NewTarget when it is absent, declaring no floor on it — the payload cannot contain a consumer-vendored Ace lib (library-stack-§6), so there is nothing to floor on — and that resolution is not a fourth edge.' Bus.lua:31-32 says Options, Media and Launcher resolve their optional libs the same way. The precedent covers libs the standard tables list (§1/§2). LCG is in neither, so §2 must gain a row first (see the standard-only candidate).
verified_consumers: DropWatcher modules/Glow.lua:201 (soft LibStub at call time), 249-270 START, 272-277 STOP, KEY 'DropWatcherUpgrade', FRAME_LEVEL 2: same semantics
QuickComms modules/Glow.lua:225, 230-251 START, 253-258 STOP, keys 'QuickCommsIcon'/'QuickCommsButton' (two keys on two frames), FRAME_LEVEL 2: same semantics (a copy of DW's)

KickCD modules/IconGrid_Render.lua:347 (LCG resolved at FILE LOAD, not call time), 374 key 'KickCD', 448-470 startEffect (same arg mapping, no frameLevel), 388-396 StopGlow (stops all four): same mapping, presentation differences only. The issue named KickCD only as a 'candidate'; it is a real consumer and the origin of the knob table (KickCD/core/Constants.lua:89-99).
AuraMaster: NOT a consumer (no LCG).
No other roster addon vendors libs/LibCustomGlow-1.0 (checked all 14).

candidates.api_sketch:
local G = LibStub('LibKa0s-Glow-1.0', true)
G.STYLES = { 'button', 'proc', 'pixel', 'autocast' }
-- knobs: { pixelLines, pixelFrequency, pixelLength (0 = auto), pixelThickness, pixelBorder,
--          autocastParticles, autocastFrequency, autocastScale, buttonFrequency,
--          procDuration, procStartAnim, xOffset, yOffset }  (nil -> the LCG default)
G.Start(frame, style, color, knobs, key, frameLevel) -> boolean started
--   resolves LibStub('LibCustomGlow-1.0', true) at CALL time; false when absent or the style's _Start is missing
G.Stop(frame, style, key)  -- style nil stops all four (KickCD's shape); button style ignores key
G.Available() -> boolean
false_or_stale_claims: 'Each consumer keeps vendoring libs/LibCustomGlow-1.0 itself': true for DW, QC and KickCD (all MINOR_VERSION 24). But the standard nowhere lists LibCustomGlow-1.0 (library-stack-§2 has no row), so the 'soft resolve' constraint has no rule to stand on yet.
candidates.recheck_trigger: Any one of these: (a) a fourth roster addon starts driving LibCustomGlow-1.0. (b) The three START/STOP copies drift: an argument-mapping fix lands in one host and not the others, or one host moves to a different LCG minor. (c) An LCG upgrade requires the same edit in all three. Re-check with the sketch above as accept-minimal.
risks: The library calls code it cannot floor-check. A host on an old LCG without ProcGlow_Start would fail inside the library, so every member needs a presence guard.
Additive-only forever: if LCG changes ProcGlow to options-only or renames arguments, the library carries the old shape.
KickCD's hot path (SPELL_STATE several times a second) must not gain a table allocation through the shared call; Start must not allocate per call.

candidates.name: Published catalogs GLOW_STYLES and GLOW_KNOBS (ranges and defaults)
candidates.rationale: The style list and the knob ranges are identical in all three hosts. That is real shared data, because it mirrors LCG's own parameters. But the issue's catalog includes defaults, and the hosts disagree on them: pixelFrequency is 0.25 in KickCD and 0.1 in DW and QC, an owner choice recorded at DropWatcher/defaults/Profile.lua:25-26. Defaults are profile-owned (savedvariables-§2: defaults/Profile.lua is the source, and KickCD's test holds its Const equal to its profile). Key spellings also disagree: KickCD uses a PascalCase leaf behind a primaryGlow/secondaryGlow prefix, while DW and QC use flat camelCase. The display order differs too: DW puts offsets first (feedback-24), QC uses DW's older order, and KickCD starts with the button knob. A shared catalog without defaults, keys or order is a 13-row range table. It belongs with the driver and should not ship alone.
candidates.bars: Bar 1: PASSES for ranges and style applicability. KickCD core/Constants.lua:100-113, DropWatcher settings/SchemaRows.lua:444-487 and QuickComms defaults/Icons.lua:29, 35-50 have the same 13 knobs, min/max/step and styles sets. It FAILS for defaults (pixelFrequency 0.25 vs 0.1). Bar 2: publishing defaults would force a per-host override, which is an escape hatch, so defaults must stay host-side. Keys would need a per-host mapping (KickCD 'leaf' vs DW/QC 'key'). Bar 3: stable while LCG's parameters are stable, so the same as the driver. A data-only catalog is low-content on its own; promoting it alone would fall under 'MUST NOT promote on frequency alone'.
verified_consumers: KickCD core/Constants.lua:100-113 Const.GLOW_KNOBS (leaf PascalCase, kind 'number', PixelFrequency default 0.25); consumed by settings/Icons.lua:337-479 and modules/IconGrid_Render.lua:405-446 (clamped)

QuickComms defaults/Icons.lua:29 GLOW_STYLES, 35-50 GLOW_KNOBS (with defaults, pixelFrequency 0.1, comment at 10-12 says 'DropWatcher's ... shared with KickCD's glow slots'); consumed by modules/IconStyle.lua:66-71 and settings/SchemaIcons.lua:185-188

candidates.name: Glow lifecycle: Glow.Apply/Stop/Release with the unchanged-repaint no-op (signature) and the proc burst spent once
candidates.rationale: The three hosts disagree on what counts as unchanged, where the effect lives, and what releases it. DW keys on kind + settings generation + button width and starts on the button itself. QC keys on a concatenated signature string (it allocates per Config) and starts on a child icon frame or an edge frame under two keys, with hover and send timers and a stand-down hook. KickCD compares four resolved color numbers plus a moved-knob flag with no allocation, because its path runs on every SPELL_STATE. A shared no-op would have to choose one policy, which is a behavior flag per consumer, a bar-2 failure. spendBurst writes LibCustomGlow's private per-frame field ('_ProcGlow'..key).startAnim. That is a coincidence of LCG minor 24's internals, not a stable abstraction (bar 3), and an additive-only library cannot carry it.
candidates.bars: Bar 1: FAILS on semantics. The trigger policy (DW KindOf 213-222, QC Wants/Sent 294-354, KickCD triggerSatisfied plus SetAlphaFromBoolean for secret notInterruptible) is host-only, as the issue concedes. The no-op policies differ: DW Glow.lua:314-318 (gen+width), QC Glow.lua:278-282 (sig string from IconStyle.lua:61-74), KickCD IconGrid_Render.lua:497-500 (four color numbers plus knobsMoved). Bar 2 ('a flag that changes what the function does is the tell'): FAILS. It would need flags for the cache key, the target frame (button vs icon frame vs edge frame), timers and release hooks. Bar 3: FAILS for spendBurst. It pokes LCG's private '_ProcGlow'..key field (LibCustomGlow-1.0.lua:858, 902, 921, 947), and KickCD does not do it at all. 'MUST NOT promote a shape whose consumers disagree about correctness': KickCD's allocation-free rule exists for performance correctness on a hot path; QC's sig allocates.
verified_consumers: DropWatcher modules/Glow.lua:285-289 spendBurst, 293-298 Stop, 305-325 Apply (gen/width), 330-332 StopFree, 336-341 Refresh (repaints NS.Window): DW-specific

KickCD modules/IconGrid_Render.lua:474-503 StartGlow (allocation-free gate), 405-446 knob clamp: KickCD-specific, no spendBurst

candidates.name: O.GlowGroup composer in LibKa0s-Options (OptionsCompose)
candidates.rationale: A composer emits the standard's canonical row set (options-ui-§15-§16: font, border, bar, color-pair, master controls). No canonical glow block exists in options-ui, so a composer would decide policy the standard has not ruled on. The three hosts also lay glow rows out in three incompatible ways. DW pairs main and off-spec side by side, with each companion below its swatch, under a documented deviation from options-ui-§17 (DropWatcher/settings/SchemaRows.lua:490-545). KickCD dims them per slot under primaryGlow/secondaryGlow PascalCase keys (KickCD/settings/Icons.lua:337-479). The issue calls BorderGroup and ColorPair the model, and they are already used for the parts that are canonical (QC SchemaIcons.lua:139 BorderGroup, 165 ColorPair).

It would need flags for pairing, hide vs dim, key prefix, offsets first, and zeroText. Bar 3: FAILS. A composer's job is to enforce a canonical block, and none exists, so the shared shape would be a coincidence of today's three pages.

verdicts.name: IconStyle half: Config / ApplyIcon / PaintBorder / PaintRing as a LibKa0s major
refutations: Line citations for the IconStyle files check out: DropWatcher/modules/IconStyle.lua is 156 lines, with QualityColor at 100, paintBorder at 110, Apply at 137 and SetTexCoord at 145. QuickComms/modules/IconStyle.lua is 175 lines, with Config at 87, ApplyIcon at 113, IconFrame at 123, PaintBorder at 135 and PaintRing at 156. The rejection stands on library-stack.md:228-241 (bars 1 to 3 and 'MUST NOT promote on frequency alone').

The only code that is the same in both hosts is the symmetric crop (DW IconStyle.lua:145 and QC IconStyle.lua:115 both call SetTexCoord(z,1-z,z,1-z)) and the borderTexture fallback (DW :71, QC :52-56, both falling back to the tooltip edge). That is low-content code, and the frequency rule keeps it inline.

One nuance: QC's own header says its code is 'modeled on DropWatcher' (QC Glow.lua:3). The same author wrote that copy within days, so a copy of a copy is not independent evidence that the abstraction is stable (bar 3). This strengthens the rejection.

verdicts.name: Stateless LibCustomGlow-1.0 driver: Start/Stop one of the four styles from a style name + knob values under a key
refutations: Every DW and QC Glow.lua citation is wrong. Each is shifted by the length of that addon's IconStyle.lua (DW +156, QC +175), which suggests the analyst read the two files concatenated. DropWatcher/modules/Glow.lua has only 185 lines: START is at 93-114 (not 249-270), STOP at 116-121 (not 272-277) and lib() is near line 45 (not 201). QuickComms/modules/Glow.lua has only 236 lines: START is at 55-76 (not 230-251), STOP at 78-83 (not 253-258) and the button-edge glow is at 189-208 (not 364-383). The KickCD citations are correct (IconGrid_Render.lua:347 LCG at file load, 374 LCG_KEY, 388-396 StopGlow, 448-470 startEffect).

'Same semantics, same traps' is overstated. Only the pixelLength 0 -> nil trap is handled the same way at all three sites (DW Glow.lua:106, QC :68, KickCD :462-463). KickCD does not coerce the rest. It passes PixelBorder raw (:464) where DW and QC use c.pixelBorder == true. It passes ProcStartAnim raw (:455) where DW and QC use ~= false. It passes XOffset/YOffset raw where DW and QC use num(v,0). It also passes no frameLevel to any style, including ProcGlow (DW and QC pass FRAME_LEVEL 2). KickCD only works because its kind='bool' schema plus clamp (Constants.lua:103,108; Render :405-446) guarantees non-nil booleans. A shared Start would make the DW/QC coercions the contract, and that contract is defensive policy from one lineage, not something all three consumers share.

There are really two lineages, not three independent consumers. QC is a declared copy of DW (QC Glow.lua:3). The DW profile says the knob set, ranges and defaults were 'shared with KickCD's glow slots (the feedback-21 plan's knob table)' (DropWatcher/defaults/Profile.lua:23-26). So the evidence is one design written twice, which is weaker than the bar-1 count of three suggests.

The api_sketch's Start(frame, style, color, knobs, key, frameLevel) takes a knobs table keyed in camelCase. KickCD stores knobs as an indexed vals array looked up through KNOB_INDEX[leaf] with PascalCase leaves (Render :448-450). To adopt it, KickCD would have to build or translate a knobs table on its hot SPELL_STATE path, or the library would need a key-mapping argument. The first breaks the analyst's own 'Start must not allocate' risk, and the second is a bar-2 escape hatch. Today KickCD's startEffect also allocates a closure and a proc options table, but only after its allocation-free gate (:474-503). A shared driver would not change that, so the hot-path claim is neutral, not a win.

Bar 3: the driver is a thin adapter to the positional signatures of LCG minor 24. The library could not floor on LCG (it is consumer-vendored), and nothing in the standard lists LCG. All three hosts are on MINOR_VERSION 24 (verified at each libs/LibCustomGlow-1.0/LibCustomGlow-1.0.lua:9). Saving about 28 lines per site at three sites does not pay for a 16th major, its docs, its tests and a module-table recount. Defer is right. On this evidence it is close to a reject with a trigger.
missed_items: QC already has two keys on two frames (KEY 'QuickCommsIcon' on qcIconFrame, BUTTON_KEY 'QuickCommsButton' on qcEdge, QC Glow.lua:44-45). KickCD's header (Render :348-372) plans the same split (LCG_KEY_PRIMARY/TARGET) and notes that ButtonGlow has no key, so two button-style glows on one frame collide. Any future driver contract must say that the button style ignores key, which the sketch does, and that two keyed callers on one frame cannot both use the button style. Leaving that out would be a correctness trap.
scope_cuts: If this is ever promoted: drop G.Available() (callers can test LibStub themselves) and drop the stop-all branch in Stop(frame, nil, key). Only KickCD uses stop-all, and it can loop over the four styles itself.

If this is ever promoted: do not bake the DW/QC coercions (num(v,0), ~= false, == true) into the contract as defaults. Map nil to nil so LCG's own defaults apply, and coerce only pixelLength 0 -> nil and pixelBorder to a boolean.
Do not name the major 'IconStyle'. Agree with the analyst's Glow naming.

verdicts.name: Published catalogs GLOW_STYLES and GLOW_KNOBS (ranges and defaults)
refutations: The ranges really are the same (KickCD core/Constants.lua:100-113 against QuickComms defaults/Icons.lua:35-50). But the three tables disagree on every axis except range: key spelling (PascalCase 'leaf' against camelCase 'key'), kind vocabulary (KickCD 'number'/'bool' against QC 'slider'/'bool'), defaults (pixelFrequency 0.25 at KickCD Constants.lua:105 against 0.1 at QC Icons.lua:37 and DW defaults/Profile.lua:33, an owner decision recorded at Profile.lua:25-26) and order. Once all of that is stripped, what remains is 13 rows of min/max/step mirroring LCG's argument ranges. That is low-content data, which the frequency rule (library-stack.md:240) keeps inline.

A range-only catalog adds a cross-repo coupling for no runtime benefit. A host still needs its own table for defaults, keys, kinds and labels, so it keeps a table either way. Deferring it as a rider on the driver risks letting it ride in later. It should be rejected now, on its own terms.
missed_items: The real drift risk is a range edited in one host only. If the owner wants protection, a cheap fix is a cross-check test in one host's suite that compares its ranges with a literal table. That needs no library surface.
scope_cuts: Even if the driver is promoted later, ship no KNOBS/STYLES catalog with it. The driver needs no catalog to work.

analysis.cluster: LibKa0s#58: a key binding for every Ka0s addon window that can be shown or hidden

candidates.name: Standard rule: the Show window entry owes a CLICK key binding (launcher-§6), plus a per-addon Bindings.xml
candidates.rationale: Everything the feature needs already exists in each addon. The toggle handler is there: each addon's launcher descriptor passes it as `toggleWindow`. The Bindings.xml shape is already settled by the standard (layout-§1, `Bindings.xml`, the client's second root file, MUST): a root file, never listed in the TOC, with no Lua body, labels set from a module. QuickComms already ships the reference implementation for its Comms Pads. What is missing is a rule that says an addon with a Show window entry owes the binding, and the addons that do not have one yet. The rule belongs in launcher.md, because that section defines the Show window entry and ADDONS.md's column is normative audit input. The column already tells an audit which addons owe a binding, so no new roster column is needed. Decided here rather than asked: (1) MUST, binding exactly the roster rows with Show window. (2) A CLICK binding on a hidden, named, non-secure Button, because a `<Binding>` body calling a global function is the Lua body layout-§1 forbids. (3) While disabled, a press prints slash-commands-§7's one refusal line (`Sl:DisabledLine()`) and toggles nothing, as QuickComms' V.TogglePads already does. Otherwise a key press on a stood-down BankLedger, LootHistory or DropWatcher does nothing and says nothing, because their show ladders refuse silently. (4) No default key is shipped. (5) The press adds no combat contract of its own: it inherits the handler's.
candidates.bars: Not a promotion question, since nothing moves into LibKa0s. The library-stack-§7 bars are judged in the helper candidate below. Rule placement was checked against the existing text. launcher.md:56 (launcher-§2) defines Show window as 'the addon's primary window ... or, for an addon with no such window, its primary display', and says a dial opened by a keybinding is not one. launcher-§2 also says 'Clicking an entry toggles it through the addon's OWN handler, the same one the slash verb and the panel row use'. The binding is one more surface onto that one handler, so the clause extends §2's one-handler rule. layout.md:101 already holds 'MUST NOT be listed in the TOC ... MUST carry no Lua script beyond what the client requires ... the labels ... (`BINDING_HEADER_*`, `BINDING_NAME_*`) are set from a module', and toc-file.md:70 says 'MUST NOT list `Bindings.xml`'. The file-shape rules therefore already exist and only the 'who owes it' rule is new.
verified_consumers: QuickComms/Bindings.xml:13 `CLICK QuickCommsTogglePads:LeftButton`. Already shipped (commit 0ee3717, 2026-10-20, on master). It is the reference shape.

QuickComms/settings/SlashVerbs.lua:85-92 builds the hidden button `QuickCommsTogglePads` with RegisterForClicks("AnyDown") and OnClick -> V.TogglePads, and rawsets the label `BINDING_NAME_CLICK QuickCommsTogglePads:LeftButton`. The handler V.TogglePads (:70-78) refuses while stood down with Sl:DisabledLine() and queues through Surfaces.Request, so it is combat-safe. Launcher QuickComms/core/LauncherSetup.lua:69 uses the same handler, so the semantics match.

QuickComms/modules/Dial.lua:52 sets `BINDING_HEADER_QUICKCOMMS = NS.BRAND`, declared in QuickComms/.luacheckrc:28. Tests: QuickComms/tests/test_dial.lua:435-483 cover the XML, the labels, the header, the TOC exclusion, and that one press runs one handler call.

BankLedger/core/LauncherSetup.lua:196-200: toggleWindow = verb("toggle"), which calls the COMMANDS row BankLedger/settings/Schema.lua:798 -> B:Toggle BankLedger/modules/Browser.lua:1120. The window is non-secure (standalone-windows), so no combat gate is needed. While stood down, B:Show silently refuses through Util.VisibilityAllows (BankLedger/core/Util.lua:266). It has no Bindings.xml today, so it owes one. Semantics match.

LootHistory/core/LauncherSetup.lua:141-145: toggleWindow = runVerb("toggle") -> LootHistory/settings/Schema.lua:1046 -> B:Toggle LootHistory/modules/Browser.lua:1124. B:Show refuses silently while stood down (:1095). It has no Bindings.xml and owes one. Semantics match.

MultiMeters/core/LauncherSetup.lua:210/288: toggleWindow = runVerb("toggle") -> doToggle MultiMeters/settings/Slash.lua:550. With no argument it toggles all windows (M:Toggle(nil), modules/WindowManager.lua:738). It has no Bindings.xml and owes one. Semantics match, because the binding is the no-argument form.

DropWatcher/core/LauncherSetup.lua:65-66: toggleWindow = NS.ToggleWindow DropWatcher/core/DropWatcher.lua:182 -> Window.Toggle DropWatcher/modules/Window.lua:814. The verb is DropWatcher/settings/Slash.lua:64. It has no Bindings.xml and owes one. Semantics match.

WhatGroup/core/LauncherSetup.lua:197-198: toggleWindow = NS.addon:ToggleFrame WhatGroup/modules/Frame.lua:1278. WhatGroup has NO `toggle` slash verb, only `show` (WhatGroup/settings/Slash.lua:43), so for WhatGroup 'the same handler as the slash verb' means the launcher's handler. Combat: the popup parents a SecureActionButtonTemplate, and ToggleFrame/dismissPopup already take the alpha-0 route with pendingHide in combat (Frame.lua:1301-1308). A key press inherits that. It has no Bindings.xml and owes one. Semantics match.

No other consumers: AbsorbTracker, AuraMaster, ConsumableMaster, KickCD, PanelMaster, PartyFrameEnhanced, PremadeGroupsFilterExtension and PrettyChat have no Show window in ADDONS.md and pass no toggleWindow (for example ConsumableMaster/core/LauncherSetup.lua:192, KickCD/core/LauncherSetup.lua:155, PanelMaster/core/LauncherSetup.lua:236 and PrettyChat/core/LauncherSetup.lua:199 each say so explicitly). PrettyChat's `BINDING_HEADER_*` hits (PrettyChat/GlobalStrings/GlobalStrings_002.lua:752+) are Blizzard GlobalStrings data, not bindings. They are a false positive and not a consumer.
false_or_stale_claims: Stale, from the issue's Scope: 'including QuickComms (Comms Pad toggle = `/qc toggle`...)', which implies QuickComms still owes the binding. It already ships it: QuickComms/Bindings.xml:13 and settings/SlashVerbs.lua:85-92, commit 0ee3717 (2026-10-20, on master), with tests test_dial.lua:463-481 and documented in README.md:30-31. QuickComms owes nothing.

Inaccurate, from the issue's Notes: 'the handler must be reachable from a global (or a CLICK ... binding on a named frame)'. The global-function option is closed by layout-§1 (layout.md:101): Bindings.xml 'MUST carry no Lua script beyond what the client requires of a `<Binding>` element'. Only the CLICK-on-a-named-frame form complies.

Inaccurate, from the issue: 'The binding calls the same handler as the slash verb'. WhatGroup has no toggle verb (WhatGroup/settings/Slash.lua:43 lists `show` only). The handler shared across all six addons is the launcher descriptor's toggleWindow.

False, from the analyst brief rather than the issue: 'TOC entry for Bindings.xml'. toc-file.md:70 says the TOC MUST NOT list Bindings.xml (layout-§1), and QuickComms' test asserts it (test_dial.lua:456-459). The per-addon change is a root file with no TOC line.

Not mentioned in the issue, and it is a correctness trap: BankLedger's and LootHistory's toggleWindow call the COMMANDS row function directly (BankLedger/core/LauncherSetup.lua:123-127, LootHistory/core/LauncherSetup.lua:78-82). That bypasses the Slash dispatcher's disabled gate (LibKa0s/LibKa0s/Slash.lua:859). The launcher is safe only because its menu grays Show window while disabled. A binding that copies that call reaches the window path with no refusal line. It is still hidden by the show ladder, but silently. The clause must therefore put the stand-down check in the binding's OnClick, or dispatch through Sl:OnSlash("toggle").
candidates.api_sketch:
No library API. Per-addon shape (QuickComms' is the reference):

Bindings.xml (root, not in TOC, no body):
  <Bindings>
    <Binding name="CLICK <Folder>Toggle<Noun>:LeftButton" header="<FOLDERUPPER>" category="ADDONS"/>
  </Bindings>

Module (beside the launcher setup, after the handler exists):
  BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER> = NS.BRAND            -- 'Ka0s <Name>'; declared in .luacheckrc globals
  local b = CreateFrame("Button", "<Folder>Toggle<Noun>", UIParent)
  b:RegisterForClicks("AnyDown")                       -- one press, one toggle
  b:SetScript("OnClick", function()
    if NS.IsStoodDown() then return NS.Print(NS.SlashCommands:DisabledLine()) end
    <the descriptor's toggleWindow handler>()
  end)
  b:Hide()
  rawset(_G, "BINDING_NAME_CLICK <Folder>Toggle<Noun>:LeftButton", L["Toggle <window>"])

Names: BankLedgerToggleWindow, LootHistoryToggleWindow, MultiMetersToggleWindows, DropWatcherToggleWindow, WhatGroupTogglePopup. QuickCommsTogglePads is unchanged. The client saves bindings by command string, so a shipped name is permanent.
libka0s_changes: None. No module or minor bump, Kit.VERSION stays at 40, and docs/api and CHANGELOG are untouched.

Record the rejection of the helper (candidate 2) as the closing comment on LibKa0s#58 when the issue is closed state:will-not-do. The issue thread is where a re-nomination will look (library-stack-§7, 'SHOULD record a rejection').

candidates.name: LibKa0s helper: a Launcher-1.0 member that names the binding header and label and builds the CLICK button routed to the descriptor's toggleWindow
candidates.rationale: The helper could own very little. The Bindings.xml file has to stay per-addon: the client reads it only from the addon's root, and the library can neither generate it nor check at runtime that the button name it creates matches the static file. What remains is about six lines: CreateFrame with a fixed name, RegisterForClicks, SetScript, Hide, one rawset label, and one header global. That is the 'high frequency plus low semantic content' shape §7 says must stay inline. A library that writes `BINDING_HEADER_*` and `BINDING_NAME_*` globals on a consumer's behalf would also split global ownership. QuickComms writes BINDING_HEADER_QUICKCOMMS from modules/Dial.lua:52 for its four dial bindings, under the same header as the pad toggle, so a helper that also set the header would collide or need an 'owns header?' flag. The helper's only real value would be enforcing the stand-down refusal and the down-edge registration. A standard clause plus each addon's own test does that just as well, and keeps the decision visible at the call site.
candidates.bars: Bar 1, 'Two or more consumers, with the same semantics — not merely the same shape': fails today. Exactly one shipped consumer exists (QuickComms/settings/SlashVerbs.lua:85-92). The other five owe the binding but have written nothing, so the claim of shared semantics would rest on code that does not exist yet. Bar 2, 'No per-consumer escape hatches ... a flag that changes what the function does is the tell': fails. QuickComms needs the header set elsewhere (Dial.lua:52, shared with four dial CLICK bindings), so the helper would need a 'do not set header' flag or an ordering contract. That flag is the divergence encoded as configuration. Bar 3, 'A stable abstraction, not a coincidence of today's code': the CLICK-binding mechanism is stable, but the button name, header and label are all per-addon presentation, and nothing about the behavior is shared beyond calling a function. Each consumer would therefore declare `Kit.bindings = {...}`, and an addon that should declare it but does not is exactly the miss the check exists to catch. The behavioral half (one press calls one handler, and a press while disabled prints the refusal line) needs Button RegisterForClicks/Click and named-frame lookup in the kit's mock_base, which has none today. QuickComms' own tests/wow_mock.lua carries them. The static half is real and generic: Bindings.xml at the root, not in the TOC, no `<Binding>` body, a BINDING_NAME_ global for every binding, and the header global equal to the brand. But it enforces layout-§1 MUSTs that already exist, with exactly one consumer today (QuickComms test_dial.lua:435-461). Bar 3 ('A stable abstraction'): the static half is stable (layout-§1 since v2.80.0, toc-file.md:70). Judged against the bars, the static half alone could pass after the rollout. challenge.cluster: LibKa0s#58: a key binding for every Ka0s addon window that can be shown or hidden

verdicts.name: Standard rule: the Show window entry owes a CLICK key binding (launcher-§6), plus a per-addon Bindings.xml
refutations: Wrong consumer claim: the analyst says LootHistory's toggleWindow 'bypasses the Slash dispatcher's disabled gate'. It does not. LootHistory/settings/Schema.lua:1023-1040 wraps every NS.COMMANDS row in gateFeatureVerbs, which prints NS.Slash.DisabledLine() when addonIsOff() before running the row (`NS.COMMANDS = gateFeatureVerbs{ ... { "toggle", ... NS.Browser:Toggle() } }`). The comment at LootHistory/core/LauncherSetup.lua:72-76 says so. A binding that calls runVerb("toggle") already refuses with the right line, so the trap is BankLedger alone. BankLedger/settings/Schema.lua:798 is an unwrapped row, and its refusal lives only in the dispatcher (BankLedger/settings/Slash.lua:331).

Wrong predicate in the proposed MUST and the api_sketch: `if NS.IsStoodDown() then return NS.Print(Sl:DisabledLine()) end`. IsStoodDown is true for the perf hold as well as the disabled hold (MultiMeters/core/LifecycleSetup.lua:283, DropWatcher/core/LifecycleSetup.lua:14, LootHistory/core/LifecycleSetup.lua:249). Three addons refuse to use it for the refusal line on purpose. MultiMeters/core/LifecycleSetup.lua:288-292 says the slash gate asks the disabled hold rather than IsStoodDown, 'because the refusal line names /mm enable and that is the wrong advice to give someone whose addon is merely mid-capture'. LootHistory/settings/Schema.lua:1013-1014 says the gate is 'deliberately not NS.IsStoodDown'. DropWatcher/core/LifecycleSetup.lua:18-20 (StoodDownRefusal) returns a separate perf line. Copying QuickComms' V.TogglePads (QuickComms/settings/SlashVerbs.lua:70), which prints the disabled line during a perf capture, would spread a wrong-message defect to five addons. The clause should say 'a press while stood down prints the same refusal line the addon's own toggle verb prints in that state (slash-commands-§7), and toggles nothing'. Each addon then reuses its existing gate: Sl:OnSlash("toggle") or the gated row in BankLedger, LootHistory, MultiMeters and DropWatcher. That keeps it 'one handler' (launcher-§2) and avoids a hand-copied second predicate.

MultiMeters already refuses on its own: M:Toggle returns false plus a message when NS.IsStoodDown() (MultiMeters/modules/WindowManager.lua:738-741), and doToggle prints it (MultiMeters/settings/Slash.lua:550-556). An OnClick-level DisabledLine check in front of that would print the wrong line mid-capture, as above. The analyst's statement that only QuickComms speaks while stood down is incomplete.

WhatGroup's combat contract is described only on the hide side. ShowFrame refuses a show in combat with its own printed line (WhatGroup/modules/Frame.lua:1236-1237: `if InCombatLockdown() and not (f and f:IsShown()) then ... _print`). WhatGroup's test must cover both cases: a press in combat with the popup off-screen prints the refusal and makes no protected call, and a press with it shown takes the alpha/pendingHide route.

Verified true: launcher.md:55-57 (launcher-§2's one handler and the Show window definition), layout.md (the Bindings.xml MUST, no TOC listing, no Lua body), ADDONS.md:21,23,25,26,31,32 (exactly six Show window rows), the toggleWindow wiring at the cited lines in all five owing addons, QuickComms/Bindings.xml:13 plus SlashVerbs.lua:85-92 on master (HEAD 12da802), and that the next free anti-pattern number is #96. Outfitter/Bindings.xml exists, but Outfitter is not on the ADDONS.md roster, so it is neither a consumer nor a precedent.
missed_items: Rule strength is the owner's call. The issue reads 'should offer' and 'If it becomes a rule', but the analyst decided on MUST plus a new audit item for five addons. Recommend MUST, since it is enumerable from ADDONS.md, but surface it to the owner rather than deciding silently.

QuickComms is not fully 'compliant, owes nothing' under the corrected refusal clause: V.TogglePads prints DisabledLine during a perf hold (QuickComms/settings/SlashVerbs.lua:70). It needs a one-line change to its own stand-down refusal (or StoodDownRefusal-style perf line), or the rule must explicitly accept it.
The layout.md paragraph says 'a CLICK binding on a secure button needs none'. When generalizing it, say non-secure as well. Otherwise the rule's 'non-secure Button' reads as contradicting layout-§1.

QuickComms' pad binding inherits the QUICKCOMMS header from the Dial1 entry and declares no header of its own (QuickComms/Bindings.xml:6 vs :13). The rule should say header= appears once per file on the first binding, and must not prescribe header= on every line as the api_sketch does.
The kit mock_base has no RegisterForClicks or Click. Each addon test re-creating QuickComms' wow_mock helpers means five more copies of that mock code. This is the cost of the deferral, so record it.
scope_cuts: Drop the mandated `NS.IsStoodDown() + DisabledLine` snippet from launcher-§6 and the api_sketch. State the behavior (same refusal line as the addon's own toggle verb) and let each addon route through its existing gate.
Drop the BankLedger/LootHistory pairing in the risk text: only BankLedger bypasses the gate.
Do not add a NEW_ADDON scaffold for Bindings.xml unless the owner confirms MUST. As a SHOULD it is a template line, not a scaffold step.

verdicts.name: LibKa0s helper: a Launcher-1.0 member that names the binding header and label and builds the CLICK button routed to the descriptor's toggleWindow
refutations: The rejection is right, and the evidence is stronger than the analyst gives. Bar 1 (library-stack.md:228-230, 'Two or more consumers, with the same semantics') fails: one shipped instance (QuickComms/settings/SlashVerbs.lua:85-92), and the five owing addons have no binding code (`ls */Bindings.xml` finds only QuickComms and the non-roster Outfitter). Bar 2 (:231-234, 'a flag that changes what the function does is the tell') fails on the refusal semantics, not only the header: the stand-down refusal disagrees across consumers (QuickComms prints DisabledLine on any IsStoodDown; MultiMeters/core/LifecycleSetup.lua:288-292, LootHistory/settings/Schema.lua:1013 and DropWatcher/core/LifecycleSetup.lua:18-20 separate disabled from perf). A helper that gated on d.isEnabled would need a refusal-message hook per consumer. That is the 'MUST NOT promote a shape whose consumers disagree about correctness' clause (:247), not only a presentation flag. 'MUST NOT promote on frequency alone ... high frequency plus low semantic content' (:240-241) also applies to a six-line constructor.

Minor: the analyst says the helper would gate 'behind d.isEnabled'. That would be wrong anyway. The launcher's isEnabled is the stored switch (e.g. DropWatcher/core/LauncherSetup.lua:59), and it says nothing about the perf hold, so the helper would toggle a window mid-capture in addons whose toggle does not self-gate (BankLedger's B:Toggle path).
missed_items: The recheck trigger should also name the case where the launcher gains a second binding-style surface that every Show window addon needs (for example a Locked toggle binding) and the per-addon refusal lines converge.
scope_cuts: Remove the 'for the record' Launcher:BindToggle sketch from launcher-§6's 'Why not a library helper' paragraph. Record the reasons only, so the sketch does not read as a ready-made API waiting for re-nomination.

verdicts.name: Test-kit check: a consumer with a Show window entry ships a conforming Bindings.xml (kit suite test_bindings)
refutations: Agree that one consumer exists today (QuickComms/tests/test_dial.lua:435-481) and that the kit cannot see ADDONS.md or the private Launcher descriptor. A kit suite now would fail Bar 1 (library-stack.md:228). Note that the trigger 'three or more addons ship Bindings.xml tests' fires automatically once the launcher-§6 rollout lands (five addons). At that point the reviewer must still check that the static assertions really agree, in particular that header= appears only once per file (QuickComms/Bindings.xml:6 vs :13). Otherwise a naive 'every Binding has header' assertion fails the reference implementation.
missed_items: The deferred static-half sketch asserts 'BINDING_HEADER_<header> == brand'. QuickComms sets it from modules/Dial.lua:52, and other addons will set it from LauncherSetup. The check must run after the full TOC load, not after a single file.
scope_cuts: Never promote the 'does this addon owe a binding' half. It stays an AUDIT.md step that reads ADDONS.md, as the analyst says.

owner_questions: Should launcher-§6 be a MUST (a new audit item and five addon rollouts) or a SHOULD? The issue says 'should offer' and 'If it becomes a rule'.

Which refusal should a key press give during a perf capture: the addon's own toggle verb's line (the perf line in MultiMeters, LootHistory and DropWatcher), or always the disabled line as QuickComms' V.TogglePads does today? The challenger recommends the former, which means a one-line QuickComms fix.

survey.revendor_procedure:
Library side (LibKa0s docs/releasing.md 'Order of operations', lines 15-232)
1. Make the change with its test. Gate: lua tests/run.lua and luacheck . (0/0, scoped by .luacheckrc).
2. Bump only the touched files' MINOR constants, never in lockstep.
3. Add new majors to tests/majors.lua.
4. Write the CHANGELOG version block. At release, replace 'unreleased' with the date.
5. Write a new docs/api/<Major>/version-<key>-docs.md for every major whose minor moved, supersede the old one, add the api/README row and run lua tools/gen-api-members.lua. test_versioning enforces this.
6. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md with lua tests/run.lua --list, keeping CRLF.
7. Move the version pointers: the releasing.md semver row and provenance template, and the README standards pointer, checked against head -1 ../WowAddonStandards/standards/STANDARDS.md. Gate, then commit. With a clean tree, run tests/_kit/run-automated-tests.sh --release <X.Y.Z>. Write ANALYSIS.md, add the release-notes line from the manifest, and commit the bundle as a second commit. Check the tag preconditions off manifest.json (release equals the version, dirty false, lint, tests and complexity pass, 0 over CCN 15, ANALYSIS.md present). Then tag. Perf is a recorded SKIP.
8. Re-vendor every consumer. This is part of the release.
9. Re-sweep the Consumers table with the LibStub grep over all 14 addons, and re-stamp docs/api/CONSUMERS.md when exports changed.

'Re-vendoring consumers' (lines 234-330), per addon
- cp -r LibKa0s/. <Addon>/libs/LibKa0s/
- diff -r --strip-trailing-cr (content, MUST be empty) and diff -r (bytes), BEFORE the prune.
- Roll the provenance line in CLAUDE.md (never README), then add `LibKa0s icons: ...` as the next non-blank line.
- lua tools/prune-icons.lua <Addon>
- cd <Addon> && lua tests/run.lua && luacheck .
- The kit (tests/_kit/ from testkit/) moves in the same commit. Payload, kit, provenance line and icon line are one atomic commit.
- Declare library-drawn icons: close, copy and clear for DebugLog hosts, and info for an id list without helpIcon.
- README attribution covers only the sets that ship (#55).
- Re-vendor from a TAG, never from master. tests/test_vendor_sync.lua resolves the tag named in the provenance line.
